Reproducing Duszkiewicz et al. (2024) from dandiset 000939¶

Paper. Duszkiewicz, Orhan, Skromne Carrasco, Brown, Owczarek, Vite, Wood and Peyrache (2024), "Local origin of excitatory-inhibitory tuning equivalence in a cortical network", Nature Neuroscience 27, 782-792, doi:10.1038/s41593-024-01588-5. The claims file (claims/000939/10.1038-s41593-024-01588-5.yaml) was written from the version of record (PMC11001581) with its Methods, Extended Data legends and Supplementary Information, and from the paper's MATLAB code on figshare (doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.24921252, version 3).

Dataset. DANDI:000939, version 0.261016.2310 (doi:10.48324/dandi.000939/0.261016.2310), 31 NWB files, one PoSub session per mouse, streamed from the archive. The paper cites no version of the dandiset (its data statement names the figshare item), so the most recent published version is pinned. Its 31 files hold the same sessions as version 0.250207.0025, with the raw voltage added in 2026; the data check below shows that the unit, spike and head-direction sample counts of every file are the same in both versions.

Outside data. Claims marked data: elsewhere in the claims file use the figshare item above, version 3: Dataset_5 (ADN recordings), Dataset_6 (optogenetic sessions with light over ADN), Dataset_4 (Neuropixel session) and Dataset_3 (cue rotation), each streamed and read in memory. Three uses serve dandiset claims without deciding them: the code's session list (SessionLists_ForAnalysis.zip) and Dataset_4 identify the session the dandiset lacks (cell-classes-counts), and the three PoSub ArchT mice of Dataset_6 that the dandiset lacks are added in a variant of the optogenetic claims.

The notebook streams about 2.7 GB of processed data from the archive and 4 GB of tarballs from figshare; it takes about 37 minutes, fifteen of them in the GLM fits.

Data check¶

import time
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import posub

T0 = time.time()
print("dandiset", posub.DANDISET, "version", posub.VERSION)
S = posub.load_all()
print(f"streamed {len(S)} files in {time.time() - T0:.0f} s")
rows = []
for s in S:
    sq = s["epochs"]["wake_square"][0]
    rem = (s["sleep"].get("rem", np.zeros((0, 2)))[:, 1] - s["sleep"].get("rem", np.zeros((0, 2)))[:, 0]).sum()
    rows.append(dict(subject=s["subject"], session=s["session_id"], orientation=s["orientation"],
                     units=len(s["spikes"]), epochs=",".join(s["epochs"]),
                     square_s=round(sq[1] - sq[0]), rem_s=round(float(rem)),
                     pulses=len(s.get("pulses", [])), virus=s["virus"][:40], genotype=s["genotype"][12:30]))
meta = pd.DataFrame(rows)
pd.set_option("display.width", 250, "display.max_columns", 20, "display.max_rows", 100)
print(meta.to_string())
print("units by orientation:", meta.groupby("orientation").units.agg(["count", "sum"]).to_dict())
# units and ranges of the variables used
hd_all = np.concatenate([s["hd"] for s in S]); pos_all = np.concatenate([s["pos"] for s in S])
print("head direction unit:", {s["hd_unit"] for s in S}, "range", np.nanmin(hd_all).round(3), np.nanmax(hd_all).round(3),
      "NaN fraction", np.isnan(hd_all).mean().round(4))
print("position unit:", {s["pos_unit"] for s in S}, "range x", np.nanmin(pos_all[:, 0]).round(1), np.nanmax(pos_all[:, 0]).round(1),
      "y", np.nanmin(pos_all[:, 1]).round(1), np.nanmax(pos_all[:, 1]).round(1))
dts = np.array([np.median(np.diff(s["hd_t"])) for s in S])
print("HD sampling interval (s), min and max over files:", dts.min().round(5), dts.max().round(5))
print("spike time resolution attribute:", {s["spike_res"] for s in S})
ttp = np.concatenate([s["ttp"] for s in S])
print("trough-to-peak (ms): n", len(ttp), "NaN", np.isnan(ttp).sum(), "range", np.nanmin(ttp), np.nanmax(ttp))
# do spikes and tracking share a clock: spikes fall inside the recording, tracking inside its epochs
for s in S:
    last = max(sp.max() for sp in s["spikes"] if len(sp)); end = max(b for v in s["epochs"].values() for a, b in v)
    assert last <= end + 1, s["subject"]
print("all spike times fall within the session's epochs")
# HD sampled only during exploration epochs?
for s in S:
    fin = np.isfinite(s["hd"]); t = s["hd_t"][fin]
    wake = [iv for k, v in s["epochs"].items() if k.startswith("wake") for iv in v]
    s["_hd_out"] = (~posub.in_intervals(t, wake)).mean()
print("fraction of tracked HD samples outside wake epochs, max over files:", max(s["_hd_out"] for s in S).round(4))
# duplicate check: identical spike trains across files
sig = {}
for s in S:
    for i, sp in enumerate(s["spikes"]):
        key = (len(sp), round(float(sp[0]), 5) if len(sp) else None, round(float(sp[-1]), 5) if len(sp) else None)
        sig.setdefault(key, []).append((s["subject"], i))
dups = {k: v for k, v in sig.items() if len(v) > 1}
print("units with identical spike count, first and last spike in two places:", len(dups))
hd_sig = {}
for s in S:
    hd_sig.setdefault((len(s["hd"]), round(float(np.nansum(s["hd"])), 3)), []).append(s["subject"])
print("files with identical HD series:", [v for v in hd_sig.values() if len(v) > 1])
# the previous published version with the same sessions (0.250207.0025, processed data only):
# units and spike counts per file, against the pinned version
import h5py, remfile
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
def _units(a):
    f = h5py.File(remfile.File(posub.s3_url(a["asset_id"])), "r")
    return a["path"].split("/")[0], len(f["units/id"]), f["units/spike_times"].shape[0], f["processing/behavior/CompassDirection/head-direction/data"].shape[0]
with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
    old = {k: (n, ns, nh) for k, n, ns, nh in ex.map(_units, posub.assets("0.250207.0025"))}
new = {s["path"].split("/")[0]: (len(s["spikes"]), sum(len(x) for x in s["spikes"]), len(s["hd"])) for s in S}
print("subjects in 0.250207.0025 and the pinned version:", len(old), len(new), "; same subjects:", set(old) == set(new))
print("files whose unit count, spike count or HD sample count differ between the versions:", [k for k in new if old.get(k) != new[k]])
# REM intervals (intervals/sleep_states): the same in 0.250207.0025 (intervals/rem there), and
# where they fall. The 2026 version says it fixed the indexing of sleep scoring epochs.
def _rem_old(a):
    f = h5py.File(remfile.File(posub.s3_url(a["asset_id"])), "r")
    if "rem" not in f["intervals"]:
        return a["path"].split("/")[0], np.zeros((0, 2))
    return a["path"].split("/")[0], np.c_[f["intervals/rem/start_time"][:], f["intervals/rem/stop_time"][:]]
with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
    rem_old = dict(ex.map(_rem_old, posub.assets("0.250207.0025")))
rem_rows = []
for s in S:
    k = s["path"].split("/")[0]
    r = s["sleep"].get("rem", np.zeros((0, 2)))
    end = max(b for v in s["epochs"].values() for a, b in v)
    smax = max(float(v.max()) for v in s["sleep"].values() if len(v))
    tt = np.arange(0, max(end, smax), 0.1)
    in_r = posub.in_intervals(tt, r)
    in_home = in_r & posub.in_intervals(tt, s["epochs"]["home_cage"])
    in_expl = in_r & posub.in_intervals(tt, [iv for t_, v in s["epochs"].items() if t_ != "home_cage" for iv in v])
    o = rem_old[k]
    rem_rows.append(dict(subject=s["subject"], session_end_s=round(end), sleep_states_end_s=round(smax), rem_s=round(float((r[:, 1] - r[:, 0]).sum())),
                         rem_in_home_cage_s=round(in_home.sum() * 0.1), rem_in_exploration_s=round(in_expl.sum() * 0.1),
                         rem_after_end_s=round((in_r & (tt >= end)).sum() * 0.1),
                         same_in_0_250207=bool(o.shape == r.shape and np.allclose(o, r))))
rem_tab = pd.DataFrame(rem_rows)
print(rem_tab.to_string())
print("files whose sleep states run past the session's end:", list(rem_tab[rem_tab.sleep_states_end_s > rem_tab.session_end_s + 5].subject),
      "; with REM inside an exploration epoch:", list(rem_tab[rem_tab.rem_in_exploration_s > 0].subject))
# the exploration epochs that hold REM, with the seconds of REM in each
for s in S:
    r = s["sleep"].get("rem", np.zeros((0, 2)))
    for tag, v in s["epochs"].items():
        ov = sum(max(0.0, min(b, y) - max(a, x)) for a, b in r for x, y in v)
        if tag != "home_cage" and ov > 0:
            print(f"{s['subject']}: {ov:.1f} s of REM inside the epoch '{tag}' {[tuple(np.round(e, 1)) for e in v]}")
# REM is used only inside the home-cage epochs (the sleep recordings, Methods); the rest is dropped
for s in S:
    r = s["sleep"].get("rem", np.zeros((0, 2)))
    clip = [(max(a, x), min(b, y)) for a, b in r for x, y in s["epochs"]["home_cage"] if min(b, y) > max(a, x)]
    s["sleep"]["rem"] = np.array(clip, float).reshape(-1, 2)
print("REM kept (s) per session, inside the home-cage epochs:", {s["subject"]: round(float((s["sleep"]["rem"][:, 1] - s["sleep"]["rem"][:, 0]).sum())) for s in S})

Tuning curves of every unit¶

Computed once for the analyses below: square-arena curves (1 degree bins, 3 degree smoothing, speed above 2 cm/s), their time-reversed controls, the two halves of the epoch, the triangle-arena curves, the 2 degree smoothing variant (code), and curves at 10 cm/s (Extended Data Fig. 3k). The time-reversed control reverses the HD series in time over the used span (the tracked square epoch, or its half) before the speed mask is applied (claims file). Rates are spike counts over the whole square epoch (code, GetMeanRates: Rate(S, wake1Ep)).

In [2]:
U = []  # one row per unit
TC = {}  # per session: dict of arrays (360, n units)
for si, s in enumerate(S):
    t, ang = s["hd_t"], s["hd"]
    a, b = s["epochs"]["wake_square"][0]
    n = len(s["spikes"])
    rate = np.array([((sp >= a) & (sp < b)).sum() / (b - a) for sp in s["spikes"]])
    m = posub.good_samples(s, "wake_square")
    d = {}
    for sd in (3, 2):
        d[f"sq{sd}"], occ = posub.tuning_curves(s["spikes"], t, ang, m, sd=sd)
        d[f"sq{sd}_rev"], occ_r = posub.tuning_curves(s["spikes"], t, ang, m, sd=sd, reverse=True)
        m1, m2 = posub.split_halves(t, m)
        d[f"h1_{sd}"], _ = posub.tuning_curves(s["spikes"], t, ang, m1, sd=sd)
        d[f"h2_{sd}"], _ = posub.tuning_curves(s["spikes"], t, ang, m2, sd=sd)
        d[f"h1_{sd}_rev"], _ = posub.tuning_curves(s["spikes"], t, ang, m1, sd=sd, reverse=True)
        d[f"h2_{sd}_rev"], _ = posub.tuning_curves(s["spikes"], t, ang, m2, sd=sd, reverse=True)
        if sd == 3:
            info = posub.hd_info(d["sq3"], occ)
            info_rev = posub.hd_info(d["sq3_rev"], occ_r)
            move_s = m.sum() * np.median(np.diff(t))
    m10 = posub.good_samples(s, "wake_square", speed_th=10.0)
    d["sq3_v10"], _ = posub.tuning_curves(s["spikes"], t, ang, m10)
    rate_tri = np.full(n, np.nan)
    if "wake_triangle" in s["epochs"]:
        ta, tb = s["epochs"]["wake_triangle"][0]
        rate_tri = np.array([((sp >= ta) & (sp < tb)).sum() / (tb - ta) for sp in s["spikes"]])
        mt = posub.good_samples(s, "wake_triangle")
        for sd in (3, 2):
            d[f"tri{sd}"], _ = posub.tuning_curves(s["spikes"], t, ang, mt, sd=sd)
            d[f"tri{sd}_rev"], _ = posub.tuning_curves(s["spikes"], t, ang, mt, sd=sd, reverse=True)
    TC[si] = d
    for i in range(n):
        U.append(dict(sess=si, subject=s["subject"], unit=i, orientation=s["orientation"], rate=rate[i],
                      rate_tri=rate_tri[i], ttp=s["ttp"][i], info=info[i], info_rev=info_rev[i],
                      lab_ex=s["lab_ex"][i], lab_fs=s["lab_fs"][i], lab_hd=s["lab_hd"][i], move_s=move_s))
U = pd.DataFrame(U)
U["gd"] = (U.rate >= posub.RATE_MIN) & np.isfinite(U.ttp)
print(f"{len(U)} units; {U.gd.sum()} viable (rate at least 0.5 Hz in the square epoch and a trough-to-peak, i.e. a negative waveform)")
print("time moving above 2 cm/s in the square epoch (s), min and max over sessions:",
      U.groupby("sess").move_s.first().min().round(0), U.groupby("sess").move_s.first().max().round(0))
print(f"tuning curves done at {time.time() - T0:.0f} s")

cell-classes-counts¶

PoSub units split into 1,835 putative excitatory cells and 427 putative FS cells by firing rate and waveform, and 1,602 excitatory cells (87%) were HD cells with HD information above 0.2 bits per spike; the vertical recordings gave 931 units from 14 mice and the parallel ones 1,999 units from 18 mice.

Classes as the claims file fixes them (Methods): viable units (rate at least 0.5 Hz in the square epoch, negative waveform, read as a finite trough-to-peak), FS below 0.4 ms and above 10 Hz, excitatory above 0.4 ms and below 10 Hz; the code's 0.35 ms cut (with its >= 10 Hz and <= 0.35 ms) is a variant. HD cells are excitatory cells above 0.2 bits per spike, and, as a second reading, above the 99th percentile of the excitatory cells' time-reversed HD information.

The parallel-probe count is compared with the code's list of the paper's 32 PoSub sessions (figshare item, SessionLists_ForAnalysis.zip, dataset_All.list), and the session the dandiset lacks is counted from figshare Dataset_4.

Result: reproduced. Under the Methods' classes there are 1,661 excitatory cells (expected 1,835 +- 184), 430 FS cells (427 +- 43), 1,512 HD cells (1,602 +- 160) and an HD fraction of 0.910 (0.87 or 0.85 +- 0.087), all within tolerance, as are the code's classes (1,699, 415, 1,532, 0.902); with the HD threshold read as the 99th percentile of the time-reversed control (0.272 bits per spike) there are 1,481 and 1,501 HD cells. The vertical recordings hold 931 units from 14 mice, as the paper gives. The parallel recordings hold 1,760 units from 17 mice, below 1,999 - 200. The session missing from the dandiset is A8603-210602, the only session of the code's list of 32 (dataset_All.list) that the dandiset lacks: the Neuropixel recording of figshare Dataset_4, with 239 units, and 1,760 + 239 = 1,999, the paper's number. So the shortfall is one session's units, the case the criterion foresees; that session is larger than any dandiset recording (185 units at most), which is why it exceeds the H5 sessions' range. The dandiset's own labels agree with the code's classes for 99.9% of units for the excitatory and FS labels and 99.7% for the HD label.

Statistics used below¶

signrank (helper) is the two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test with its normal-approximation z (MATLAB's signrank reports this z); ranksum (helper) is the two-sided Mann-Whitney U test with its z. All tests are two-tailed (Methods).

In [4]:

def per_unit(key):
    """Stack a per-session curve array over all units, in the order of U."""
    return np.concatenate([TC[si][key] for si in range(len(S))], axis=1)

for sd in (3, 2):
    r = posub.zero_lag_r(per_unit(f"h1_{sd}"), per_unit(f"h2_{sd}"))
    rr = posub.zero_lag_r(per_unit(f"h1_{sd}_rev"), per_unit(f"h2_{sd}_rev"))
    U[f"r_half{sd}"], U[f"r_half{sd}_rev"] = r, rr

fig2c-geometry-independent¶

The tuning of PoSub-FS cells is preserved between the square and triangular arenas, as it is for PoSub-HD cells.

Sessions with a triangle epoch. FS cells above 10 Hz and HD cells above 0.5 Hz in both arenas (criterion; code Figure_Stability). Each session's triangle curves are shifted back by the circular mean of its HD cells' rotations (lag of maximum square-triangle cross-correlation; Methods). The control shifts the time-reversed triangle curves by the same amount and correlates them with the time-reversed square curves.

In [8]:
tri_rows = []
for sd in (3, 2):
    rs, rc = [], []
    for si, s in enumerate(S):
        if f"tri{sd}" not in TC[si]:
            continue
        u = U[U.sess == si]
        hdm = (u.hd & (u.rate > 0.5) & (u.rate_tri > 0.5)).values
        fsm = (u.fs & (u.rate > 10) & (u.rate_tri > 10)).values
        sq, tr = TC[si][f"sq{sd}"], TC[si][f"tri{sd}"]
        sqr, trr = TC[si][f"sq{sd}_rev"], TC[si][f"tri{sd}_rev"]
        lag = posub.circ_xcorr_lag(sq[:, hdm], tr[:, hdm])
        rot = int(np.round(np.rad2deg(stats.circmean(np.deg2rad(lag))))) % 360
        tr_s, trr_s = np.roll(tr, -rot, axis=0), np.roll(trr, -rot, axis=0)
        for cls, m in (("HD", hdm), ("FS", fsm)):
            r = posub.zero_lag_r(sq[:, m], tr_s[:, m]); c = posub.zero_lag_r(sqr[:, m], trr_s[:, m])
            tri_rows += [dict(sd=sd, cls=cls, subject=s["subject"], rot=rot, r=a, r_rev=b) for a, b in zip(r, c)]

        show(signrank(d.r, d.r_rev), f"{cls}, smoothing {sd} deg:")

fig2b-decoding-from-fs¶

The animal's HD can be decoded accurately from PoSub-FS cell spiking with a Bayesian decoder built on their tuning curves, and decoding error falls as more FS cells are used.

As GetBayesianDecoding.m (criterion): the square epoch from first to last tracked sample is split into two halves of equal time; tuning curves (360 bins, 3 degree smoothing) from the first half at speed above 2 cm/s; spike counts in 100 ms bins smoothed with a Gaussian of 2 bins s.d.; decoding over the second half, all times; error the absolute angular difference from the real HD sample nearest each bin centre, median per session. Chance: the same with tuning curves built from the HD time-reversed over the epoch, its error also taken from the real HD (criterion).

In [9]:
from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
dec = []
for si, s in enumerate(S):
    u = U[U.sess == si]
    t, ang = s["hd_t"], s["hd"]
    a, b = posub.tracked_epoch(s, "wake_square")
    in_ep = (t >= a) & (t <= b)
    ang_rev = ang.copy(); ang_rev[in_ep] = ang[in_ep][::-1]
    mid = (a + b) / 2
    m1 = posub.good_samples(s, "wake_square") & (t < mid)
    edges = np.arange(a, b, 0.1); cen = edges[:-1] + 0.05
    sec = cen >= mid
    j = np.clip(np.searchsorted(t, cen[sec]), 1, len(t) - 1); j = np.where(np.abs(t[j - 1] - cen[sec]) < np.abs(t[j] - cen[sec]), j - 1, j)
    row = dict(subject=s["subject"], n_fs=int(u.fs.sum()), n_hd=int(u.hd.sum()))
    for cls in ("fs", "hd"):
        idx = np.where(u[cls].values)[0]
        if len(idx) == 0:
            continue
        sp = [s["spikes"][i] for i in idx]
        Q = gaussian_filter1d(posub.bin_counts(sp, edges), 2, axis=0)
        for kind, aa in (("real", ang), ("rev", ang_rev)):
            tc, _ = posub.tuning_curves(sp, t, aa, m1 & np.isfinite(aa))
            th = np.deg2rad(posub.bayes_decode(tc, Q[sec], 0.1))
            err = np.abs(posub.angdiff(th, ang[j]))  # both decoders scored against the real HD
            ok = np.isfinite(ang[j])
            row[f"{cls}_{kind}"] = np.rad2deg(np.median(err[ok]))
    dec.append(row)
dec = pd.DataFrame(dec)
print(dec.round(1).to_string())
print(f"mean over {len(dec)} sessions of median error (deg): FS {dec.fs_real.mean():.1f}, FS chance {dec.fs_rev.mean():.1f}, "
      f"HD {dec.hd_real.mean():.1f}, HD chance {dec.hd_rev.mean():.1f}")
show(signrank(dec.fs_real, dec.fs_rev), "FS error vs chance, per session:")
r, p = stats.pearsonr(dec.n_fs, dec.fs_real)
print(f"Pearson r between number of FS cells and FS median error = {r:.3f}, p = {p:.3g}, n = {len(dec)}")
rs, ps = stats.spearmanr(dec.n_fs, dec.fs_real)
print(f"(Spearman, shown only: rho = {rs:.3f}, p = {ps:.3g})")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4, 3)); ax.scatter(dec.n_fs, dec.fs_real); ax.set_xlabel("FS cells"); ax.set_ylabel("median error (deg)"); plt.show()
print("plotted ranges: cells", dec.n_fs.min(), dec.n_fs.max(), "error", dec.fs_real.min().round(1), dec.fs_real.max().round(1))

Result: reproduced. Over 31 sessions the mean of the FS decoder's median error is 36.0 degrees against a chance level of 92.8 (both scored against the real HD; signed-rank over sessions p = 1.3e-6), and the error falls with the number of FS cells (Pearson r = -0.449, p = 0.011, n = 31). The HD-cell decoder's mean median error is 9.9 degrees.

fig2f-cue-rotation (figshare, data elsewhere)¶

In a cue rotation task PoSub-FS cell tuning curves follow the rotated distal landmark together with PoSub-HD cells.

The six cue rotation sessions are figshare Dataset_3.tar.gz (claims file), streamed here. Cell classes are the files' own CellTypes (hd, fs). Methods (Analysis of HD cell realignment after cue rotation): HD cell spikes in 50 ms bins smoothed with 100 ms s.d.; Bayesian decoding with tuning curves (1 degree bins, 3 degree smoothing) from the baseline period with a stable cue (LED1 first interval, as GetBayesianDecoding_CueRotation.m); decoder error the angular difference between real and decoded HD. Rotations at the starts of the 16 cue epochs (CueEpochs.mat). Exclusion (criterion): (1) the circular mean decoder error over the 200 s after the rotation differs by less than 45 degrees from that over the 200 s before it (the change, as the code computes it, since the cue returns to its first wall every second rotation); (2) mean speed below 2 cm/s in the preceding epoch (positions from Tracking_data.csv, metres). Main reading excludes a rotation failing either; the second reading only one failing both. A sigmoid is fitted to the decoder error (re-centred on the preceding epoch's mean error) from 50 s before to 200 s after each rotation; realignment ends where the normalized sigmoid reaches 0.99. For each cell, a tuning curve (1 degree, 3 degree smoothing, no speed threshold) over the rest of each epoch; its realignment is the lag of maximum cross-correlation with the curve of the preceding epoch. Per FS cell, the mean absolute difference between its realignment and the circular mean realignment of the session's HD cells, over the kept rotations; control, the same with the FS curves from the time-reversed HD; Wilcoxon signed-rank.

In [10]:
from scipy.optimize import curve_fit
CU = posub.load_adn(file_id=posub.FIGSHARE_CUE_FILE)
sigm = lambda x, a, b, c, d: a + (b - a) / (1 + 10 ** ((c - x) * d))
cue_rows, rot_rows = [], []
for c in CU:
    t, ang = c["hd_t"], c["hd"]
    hdc = np.where(c["file_types"]["hd"])[0]; fsc = np.where(c["file_types"]["fs"])[0]
    b0, b1 = c["led1"][0]
    mb = posub.in_intervals(t, [(b0, b1)]) & np.isfinite(ang)
    tc_b, _ = posub.tuning_curves([c["spikes"][i] for i in hdc], t, ang, mb)
    wa, wb = c["eps"]["wakeEp"][0]
    edges = np.arange(wa, wb, 0.05); cen = edges[:-1] + 0.025
    Q = gaussian_filter1d(posub.bin_counts([c["spikes"][i] for i in hdc], edges), 2, axis=0)
    dec = np.deg2rad(posub.bayes_decode(tc_b, Q, 0.05))
    j = np.clip(np.searchsorted(t, cen), 1, len(t) - 1); j = np.where(np.abs(t[j - 1] - cen) < np.abs(t[j] - cen), j - 1, j)
    real = np.where(np.abs(t[j] - cen) < 0.02, ang[j], np.nan)
    err = posub.angdiff(real, dec)
    tr = c["track"]; _, uq = np.unique(tr[:, 0], return_index=True); tr = tr[uq]  # repeated timestamps dropped
    tt = tr[:, 0]; xy = tr[:, 1:3] * 100
    sp_ = np.r_[0, np.hypot(*np.diff(gaussian_filter1d(xy, 10, axis=0), axis=0).T) / np.diff(tt)]
    ce = c["cueEp"]
    starts = ce[:, 0]
    cmean = lambda x: np.angle(np.nanmean(np.exp(1j * x[np.isfinite(x)])))
    for k, r0 in enumerate(starts):
        pre = (cen >= r0 - 200) & (cen < r0); post = (cen >= r0) & (cen < r0 + 200)
        change = abs(np.rad2deg(posub.angdiff(cmean(err[post]), cmean(err[pre]))))
        prev_speed = sp_[(tt >= r0 - 200) & (tt < r0)].mean()
        w = (cen >= r0 - 50) & (cen < r0 + 200) & np.isfinite(err)
        x = cen[w]; y = np.rad2deg(posub.angdiff(err[w], cmean(err[pre])))
        try:
            p, _ = curve_fit(sigm, x, y, p0=[np.quantile(y, 0.05), np.quantile(y, 0.95), r0 + 10, 0.1], maxfev=20000)
            yv = sigm(x, *p); yn = (yv - yv.min()) / (yv.max() - yv.min())
            if yv[0] > yv[-1]:
                yn = 1 - yn
            end = x[np.argmin(np.abs(yn - 0.99))]
        except Exception:
            end = np.nan
        # the code's rule (GetSigmoids_CueRotation.m): windows of the last 50 s of each epoch
        w_pre = (cen >= r0 - 50) & (cen < r0); w_post = (cen >= r0 + 150) & (cen < r0 + 200)
        code_change = abs(np.rad2deg(posub.angdiff(cmean(err[w_post]), cmean(err[w_pre]))))
        e_ = err[w_pre][np.isfinite(err[w_pre])]
        code_var = np.rad2deg(1 - np.abs(np.mean(np.exp(1j * e_))))
        mh = (t >= r0 - 50) & (t < r0) & np.isfinite(ang)
        ahv = np.nanmean(np.abs(np.rad2deg(np.diff(np.unwrap(ang[mh]))) / np.diff(t[mh])))
        rot_rows.append(dict(session=c["session"], k=k, change=change, prev_speed=prev_speed, end_s=end - r0 if np.isfinite(end) else np.nan,
                             code_change=code_change, code_var=code_var, ahv=ahv))
    R = pd.DataFrame([r for r in rot_rows if r["session"] == c["session"]])
    # tuning curves over the rest of each epoch (from the end of realignment), and the epoch before the first rotation
    segs = [(starts[0] - 200, starts[0])] + [((r0 + (e if np.isfinite(e) else 0)), ce[k, 1]) for k, (r0, e) in enumerate(zip(starts, R.end_s))]
    cells = np.r_[hdc, fsc]
    H = []; Hr = []
    for a_, b_ in segs:
        m = posub.in_intervals(t, [(a_, b_)]) & np.isfinite(ang)
        H.append(posub.tuning_curves([c["spikes"][i] for i in cells], t, ang, m)[0])
        Hr.append(posub.tuning_curves([c["spikes"][i] for i in cells], t, ang, m, reverse=True)[0])
    nh = len(hdc)
    for k in range(len(starts)):
        lag = posub.circ_xcorr_lag(H[k], H[k + 1]); lag_r = posub.circ_xcorr_lag(Hr[k], Hr[k + 1])
        hd_mean = stats.circmean(np.deg2rad(lag[:nh][np.isfinite(lag[:nh])]))
        for jj, i in enumerate(fsc):
            d = abs(np.rad2deg(posub.angdiff(np.deg2rad(lag[nh + jj]), hd_mean)))
            dr = abs(np.rad2deg(posub.angdiff(np.deg2rad(lag_r[nh + jj]), hd_mean)))
            cue_rows.append(dict(session=c["session"], cell=i, k=k, diff=d, diff_rev=dr,
                                 hd_rot=np.rad2deg(hd_mean) % 360, change=R.change[k], prev_speed=R.prev_speed[k],
                                 code_change=R.code_change[k], code_var=R.code_var[k], ahv=R.ahv[k]))
ROT = pd.DataFrame(rot_rows); CR = pd.DataFrame(cue_rows)
print(ROT.round(1).to_string())
print("rotations failing: change < 45:", int((ROT.change < 45).sum()), "; speed < 2 cm/s:", int((ROT.prev_speed < 2).sum()), "; realignment end (s) median", ROT.end_s.median().round(1), "range", ROT.end_s.min().round(1), ROT.end_s.max().round(1))
for name, excl in (("main: exclude a rotation failing either condition", lambda d: (d.change < 45) | (d.prev_speed < 2)),
                   ("second: exclude only a rotation failing both", lambda d: (d.change < 45) & (d.prev_speed < 2)),
                   ("change condition alone", lambda d: d.change < 45),
                   ("code variant: change < 45, variance > 10 or AHV < 10", lambda d: (d.code_change < 45) | (d.code_var > 10) | (d.ahv < 10))):
    kept = CR[~excl(CR)]
    per = kept.groupby(["session", "cell"])[["diff", "diff_rev"]].mean()
    print(f"{name}: rotations kept {int((~excl(ROT)).sum())} of {len(ROT)}; FS cells {len(per)}")
    show(signrank(per["diff"], per["diff_rev"]), "   FS minus HD realignment |difference| (deg), real vs control:")
print("paper: n = 99 FS cells, z = 8.25")
print("HD rotation (deg) at kept rotations, main reading:", CR[~((CR.change < 45) | (CR.prev_speed < 2))].groupby(["session", "k"]).hd_rot.first().round(0).values)

Result: reproduced. In the six figshare cue rotation sessions, the realignment of the 99 FS cells is closer to that of the HD cells than in the time-reversed control (median absolute difference 36.2 against 91.8 degrees, |z| = 8.57, p = 1e-17; paper z = 8.25), with 89 of 96 rotations kept under the main exclusion reading, and the same under the other readings and the code's rule (|z| 8.58 to 8.59). The HD cells rotate by about 90 and 270 degrees at the kept rotations.

Fourier spectra¶

Each 360-bin tuning curve (3 degree smoothing) is projected on harmonics 1 to 180 (code, Figure_Fourier). Power is read two ways (claims file): the squared modulus of the complex coefficient (code) and the root mean square of the sine and cosine projections (Methods' words). The first ten powers are normalized to their sum.

In [11]:
H = per_unit("sq3"); H_rev = per_unit("sq3_rev")
FT, FT_rev = posub.fourier(H), posub.fourier(H_rev)
P = {rd: posub.power(FT, rd) for rd in ("sq", "rms")}
P_rev = {rd: posub.power(FT_rev, rd) for rd in ("sq", "rms")}
N10 = {rd: posub.norm10(P[rd]) for rd in P}
N10_rev = {rd: posub.norm10(P_rev[rd]) for rd in P}
fsm, hdm = U.fs.values, U.hd.values
# Parseval check (Extended Data Fig. 3e): 2 x sum of squared moduli = variance of the curve
pv = 2 * P["sq"].sum(0) / H.var(0)
print("Parseval, 2 x sum |c_k|^2 over the curve's variance: median", np.nanmedian(pv[fsm | hdm]).round(4),
      "range", np.nanmin(pv[fsm | hdm]).round(4), np.nanmax(pv[fsm | hdm]).round(4))

Parseval, 2 x sum |c_k|^2 over the curve's variance: median 1.0 range 1.0 1.0

fig3-ten-components-power¶

Fourier power of tuning curves decays quickly with frequency, and the first ten components hold on average 98% of the total power.

Expected 0.98, tolerance 0.02. Readings: population (a) FS and HD pooled, (b) each alone; power (a) squared modulus, (b) root mean square. Reproduced when one population reading under each power reading is within tolerance.

In [12]:
rows = []
for rd in ("sq", "rms"):
    frac = P[rd][:10].sum(0) / P[rd].sum(0)
    for pop, m in (("FS + HD", fsm | hdm), ("FS", fsm), ("HD", hdm)):
        rows.append(dict(power=rd, population=pop, n=int(m.sum()), mean_fraction=frac[m].mean().round(4),
                         within=abs(frac[m].mean() - 0.98) <= 0.02))
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string())
mp = P["sq"][:, fsm | hdm].mean(1)
print("mean squared-modulus power, harmonics 1 to 12, relative to harmonic 1:", (mp[:12] / mp[0]).round(4))

 0.0019 0.0017]

Result: partially reproduced. With power as the squared modulus (the code, and the only reading under which the Parseval check holds, ratio 1.0000), the first ten harmonics hold on average 0.989 of the power of FS and HD cells pooled, 0.969 for FS and 0.994 for HD cells, all within 0.98 +- 0.02, and the mean power falls to 0.10 of the first harmonic's by the fifth. With power as the root mean square of the projections (the Methods' words) the fractions are 0.872, 0.778 and 0.898, none within tolerance, and the criterion asks for one population within tolerance under each power reading.

fig3g-first-three-components¶

Compared with time-reversed controls, the PoSub-FS spectrum has higher power for the first three Fourier components only.

Repeated-measures ANOVA, condition (real, time-reversed) by component (1 to 10), within cells; then a Wilcoxon signed-rank test per component with p multiplied by 10 (criterion; code).

In [13]:
from statsmodels.stats.anova import AnovaRM
for rd in ("sq", "rms"):
    a, b = N10[rd][:, fsm], N10_rev[rd][:, fsm]
    n = a.shape[1]
    long = pd.DataFrame(dict(cell=np.tile(np.repeat(np.arange(n), 10), 2), comp=np.tile(np.tile(np.arange(1, 11), n), 2),
                             cond=np.repeat(["real", "rev"], 10 * n), y=np.r_[a.T.ravel(), b.T.ravel()]))
    res = AnovaRM(long, "y", "cell", within=["cond", "comp"]).fit().anova_table
    print(f"power {rd}: interaction F({int(res.loc['cond:comp', 'Num DF'])},{int(res.loc['cond:comp', 'Den DF'])}) = "
          f"{res.loc['cond:comp', 'F Value']:.1f}, p = {res.loc['cond:comp', 'Pr > F']:.3g}")
    out = []
    for k in range(10):
        d = signrank(a[k], b[k])
        out.append(dict(component=k + 1, real_median=round(d["median_a"], 4), rev_median=round(d["median_b"], 4),
                        z=round(d["z"], 2), z_over_10=round(d["z"] / 10, 3), p_bonf=min(1, d["p"] * 10),
                        higher=d["median_a"] > d["median_b"]))
    out = pd.DataFrame(out); print(out.to_string())
    sig_hi = out[(out.p_bonf < 0.05) & out.higher].component.tolist()
    sig_hi_mean = [k + 1 for k in range(10) if out.p_bonf[k] < 0.05 and a[k].mean() > b[k].mean()]
    print(f"power {rd}: components significantly higher than control (medians): {sig_hi}; (means): {sig_hi_mean}")
print("paper: F(9,3834) = 64.1, p = 4e-110; components 1 to 3 higher (p = 8e-10, 3e-16, 4e-5)")

Result: partially reproduced. The condition by component interaction is significant under both power readings (squared modulus F(9,3861) = 122.9, p = 1e-203; root mean square F = 227.2; paper F(9,3834) = 64.1). After Bonferroni correction, with squared-modulus power components 1 and 2 are higher than control (p = 4e-28 and 8e-20) and component 3 is higher in median (0.114 against 0.093) but not significantly (p = 0.064); with root-mean-square power components 1 to 4 are higher (component 4, p = 0.003). The criterion's set, components 1, 2 and 3 and no other, holds under neither power reading; the FS spectrum is above control at the lowest components and below it from component 5 on under both.

fig3h-dominant-component¶

Of the 427 PoSub-FS cells, 231, 141 and 55 have their highest power in the first, second and third Fourier component, proportions similar to the relative mean power of those components.

Each FS cell goes to the largest of its first three powers (code, highComp). Readings of "similar": (a) the proportions are in the same order as the mean relative powers of components 1 to 3 renormalized over those three; (b) each proportion is within 10% of its renormalized mean power (read as a relative 10%; an absolute 0.10 is shown too).

In [14]:
high = np.argmax(N10["sq"][:3], axis=0) + 1
U["high"] = high
cnt = pd.Series(high[fsm]).value_counts().sort_index()
print("FS cells by dominant component (1, 2, 3):", cnt.to_dict(), "of", int(fsm.sum()), "; expected 231 +-23, 141 +-14, 55 +-6")
print("same assignment under the rms reading:", bool((np.argmax(N10["rms"][:3], 0)[fsm] == high[fsm] - 1).all()))
prop = cnt.values / cnt.sum()
for rd in ("sq", "rms"):
    mpw = N10[rd][:3, fsm].mean(1); mpw = mpw / mpw.sum()
    a_ok = list(np.argsort(-prop)) == list(np.argsort(-mpw))
    rel = np.abs(prop - mpw) / mpw
    print(f"power {rd}: proportions {prop.round(3)}, renormalized mean powers {mpw.round(3)}; (a) same order: {a_ok}; "
          f"(b) relative differences {rel.round(3)}, all within 10%: {bool((rel <= 0.10).all())}; absolute differences {np.abs(prop - mpw).round(3)}")
print("per subject, FS cells by dominant component:")
print(U[U.fs].groupby("subject").high.value_counts().unstack(fill_value=0).T.to_string())

Result: not reproduced. FS cells peak in component 1, 2 and 3 in 237, 146 and 47 cases; the first two are within tolerance of 231 and 141, the third is below 55 - 6. The criterion's reproduced and partial outcomes both need all counts within tolerance, so the claim is not reproduced. The proportions (0.551, 0.340, 0.109) are in the same order as the renormalized mean powers (0.486, 0.326, 0.187), reading (a), but differ by more than 10% for components 1 and 3 (13% and 42%), reading (b), under both power readings. The dandiset has 430 FS cells where the paper has 427.

ed3g-fs-spectra-heterogeneous¶

Fourier signatures are far more variable among PoSub-FS cells than among HD cells of the same region, so individual FS cells are narrowly tuned in Fourier space.

Distance of each cell's ten-component spectrum from its own population's mean: Euclidean (code, ftDist) and KL divergence D_KL(cell || mean) (legend, Methods direction), both power readings. FS against PoSub-HD, Mann-Whitney U, p multiplied by 3. The ANOVA and the ADN-HD comparisons are in the ADN section below.

In [15]:
DIST = {}
for rd in ("sq", "rms"):
    for meas in ("euclid", "kl"):
        d = np.full(len(U), np.nan)
        for m in (fsm, hdm):
            mu = N10[rd][:, m].mean(1, keepdims=True)
            d[m] = np.sqrt(((N10[rd][:, m] - mu) ** 2).sum(0)) if meas == "euclid" else posub.kl(N10[rd][:, m], mu)
        DIST[(rd, meas)] = d
        r = ranksum(d[fsm], d[hdm]); r["p_x3"] = min(1, r["p"] * 3); r["z_over_3"] = r["z"] / 3
        show(r, f"power {rd}, {meas}: FS vs PoSub-HD")
print("paper: legend z = 5.71 (a third of the test's z)")

ed3l-fs-phases-independent¶

Phases of the Fourier components are correlated with each other in individual HD cells but random relative to each other in PoSub-FS cells.

Circular correlation (circ_corrcc) across cells between twice the first phase (mod 2 pi) and the second phase, and three times the first and the third (criterion; code).

In [16]:
ph = np.angle(FT[:3])
for name, m in (("PoSub-HD", hdm), ("PoSub-FS", fsm)):
    for k in (2, 3):
        rho, p = posub.circ_corrcc(np.mod(k * ph[0, m], 2 * np.pi), np.mod(ph[k - 1, m], 2 * np.pi))
        print(f"{name}: {k} x phase 1 against phase {k}: rho = {rho:.3f}, p = {p:.3g}, n = {int(m.sum())}")
# the FS result with code classes
exc_, fsc_ = classify(U, 0.35, True)
for k in (2, 3):
    rho, p = posub.circ_corrcc(np.mod(k * ph[0, fsc_.values], 2 * np.pi), np.mod(ph[k - 1, fsc_.values], 2 * np.pi))
    print(f"PoSub-FS, code classes: {k} x phase 1 against phase {k}: rho = {rho:.3f}, p = {p:.3g}")

PoSub-HD: 2 x phase 1 against phase 2: rho = 0.322, p = 0, n = 1512
PoSub-HD: 3 x phase 1 against phase 3: rho = 0.087, p = 9.79e-05, n = 1512
PoSub-FS: 2 x phase 1 against phase 2: rho = 0.014, p = 0.768, n = 430
PoSub-FS: 3 x phase 1 against phase 3: rho = 0.005, p = 0.913, n = 430
PoSub-FS, code classes: 2 x phase 1 against phase 2: rho = 0.006, p = 0.902
PoSub-FS, code classes: 3 x phase 1 against phase 3: rho = -0.016, p = 0.738

Result: reproduced. Across PoSub-HD cells twice the first phase is correlated with the second (rho = 0.32, p < 1e-15) and three times the first with the third (rho = 0.087, p = 1e-4); across FS cells neither is (rho = 0.014, p = 0.77; rho = 0.005, p = 0.91), nor with the code's classes (p = 0.90 and 0.74).

ADN recordings (figshare, claims with data elsewhere)¶

The ADN-HD cells of Fig. 3 are not in the dandiset. The claims file names their source, the paper's figshare item doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.24921252 version 3, Dataset_5.tar.gz. It is streamed and read in memory (helper load_adn). Tuning curves are computed from the spike times, head direction and the file's speed as for PoSub; ADN-HD cells are units with rate above 0.5 Hz and HD information at least 0.2 bits per spike (code, GetCellTypes_ADN), among units the file's BrainArea marks as ADN (code, Figure_Fourier isAdn).

In [18]:
A = posub.load_adn()
print("ADN sessions:", len(A), "; units:", sum(len(a["spikes"]) for a in A), "; marked ADN:", sum(int(a["adn"].sum()) for a in A))
ADN = []
for a in A:
    d = posub.adn_tuning(a)
    d10 = posub.adn_tuning(a, speed_th=10.0)
    hd = a["adn"] & (d["rate"] > 0.5) & (d["info"] >= 0.2)
    d.update(hd=hd, h10=d10["h"], file_hd=a["file_hd"], session=a["session"])
    ADN.append(d)
adn_hd = np.concatenate([d["hd"] for d in ADN]); adn_file = np.concatenate([d["file_hd"] for d in ADN])
print("ADN-HD cells recomputed:", int(adn_hd.sum()), "; in the files' CellTypes:", int(adn_file.sum()),
      "; agreement:", (adn_hd == adn_file).mean().round(3), "; paper: 97")
HA = np.concatenate([d["h"][:, d["hd"]] for d in ADN], 1)
HA_rev = np.concatenate([d["h_rev"][:, d["hd"]] for d in ADN], 1)
HA10 = np.concatenate([d["h10"][:, d["hd"]] for d in ADN], 1)
HA1 = np.concatenate([d["h1"][:, d["hd"]] for d in ADN], 1); HA2 = np.concatenate([d["h2"][:, d["hd"]] for d in ADN], 1)
adn_sess = np.concatenate([[d["session"]] * int(d["hd"].sum()) for d in ADN])
# contamination scores, ADN-HD
adn_cq = np.concatenate([[posub.contamination(sp) for sp, k in zip(a["spikes"], d["hd"]) if k] for a, d in zip(A, ADN)])

fig3e-fourier-signatures-differ¶

The average Fourier signatures of PoSub-FS, PoSub-HD and ADN-HD populations differ, with ADN-HD cells having more power at low and less at high components than PoSub-HD and PoSub-FS cells, which are alike.

Repeated-measures ANOVA of the ten normalized powers, component by cell type interaction, cell type as a numeric covariate (code: FS 1, PoSub-HD 2, ADN-HD 3) and, as a variant, as a categorical factor. Direction readings (a) ADN mean above both PoSub means at component 1 and below both summed over components 3 to 10; (b) ADN cumulative signature above both at every component 1 to 9. Both power readings.

Result: partially reproduced. The direction holds under both direction readings and both power readings: the ADN-HD signature has more power at component 1 than both PoSub signatures (0.509 against 0.398 and 0.358, squared modulus) and less over components 3 to 10, and its cumulative signature is above both at components 1 to 9, the ones tested (at component 10 all three equal 1). The interaction is not significant under the main reading, squared-modulus power with cell type as the code's numeric covariate (F(9,18333) = 1.09, p = 0.365; paper F(9,19116) = 2.76, p = 0.003). It is significant with root-mean-square power (F = 10.68, p = 1e-16) and with cell type as a categorical factor (F(18,18324) = 24.7, p = 5e-82, and 44.6, p = 2e-155). The criterion's test thus holds under some readings and not under the one that follows the code. A numeric code tests a linear trend from FS through PoSub-HD to ADN-HD, and FS and ADN-HD both lie above PoSub-HD at component 1, which such a trend does not capture. The PoSub-only ANOVA, a variant, gives F(9,17460) = 11.4, p = 6e-18.

fig3f-posub-hd-closer-to-fs¶

Individual PoSub-HD cell Fourier spectra are closer to the average PoSub-FS signature than ADN-HD cell spectra are.

KL divergence between each HD cell's ten-component spectrum and the mean PoSub-FS spectrum, both directions and both power readings; Mann-Whitney U, PoSub-HD against ADN-HD.

In [21]:
def fs_distance(rd, Npos, Nadn, Nfs, direction):
    S_ = Nfs.mean(1, keepdims=True)
    f = (lambda c: posub.kl(c, S_)) if direction == "cell||FS" else (lambda c: posub.kl(np.broadcast_to(S_, c.shape), c))
    return f(Npos), f(Nadn)

F3F = {}
for rd in ("sq", "rms"):
    for direction in ("cell||FS", "FS||cell"):
        dp, da = fs_distance(rd, N10[rd][:, hdm], NA[rd], N10[rd][:, fsm], direction)
        r = ranksum(dp, da); F3F[(rd, direction)] = r
        show(r, f"power {rd}, D_KL({direction}): PoSub-HD vs ADN-HD")
print("paper: p < 1e-9, n = 1602 and 97")

Result: partially reproduced. PoSub-HD spectra are closer to the mean FS spectrum than ADN-HD spectra under all four readings (median KL 0.082 against 0.133, 0.106 against 0.233, 0.050 against 0.090 and 0.063 against 0.125), with p = 0.008 (squared modulus, D_KL(cell||FS), the Methods' direction), 1e-7, 1.8e-9 and 3e-12. The p-value is below 1e-9 under one reading only, the criterion's partial outcome.

ed3k-robust-to-controls¶

The smaller distance of PoSub-HD than ADN-HD spectra from the PoSub-FS signature holds after excluding multipeaked HD cells, after excluding noisy clusters, and with a 10 cm/s speed threshold; multipeak scores differ between ADN-HD and PoSub-HD cells.

The Fig. 3f test under each control and each reading. Multipeak score below 0.05 (HD cells; code), contamination score at most 0.2 (all cells, as the code's onlyGoodClusters filters HD, FS and viable cells), curves at speed above 10 cm/s (all cells).

The statement was amended after a reader's answer (questions/000939.yaml): the paper gives no direction for the multipeak test, so the criterion accepts it at p < 0.05 in either direction; the three Fourier distance tests keep the paper's direction (PoSub-HD closer, z < 0 here).

cq_pos = U.cq.values

    for direction in ("cell||FS", "FS||cell"):

The multipeak scores differ (z = -4.18, p = 3e-5; paper z = 4.25), with ADN-HD cells scoring lower than PoSub-HD cells (median 0.022 against 0.049), as the paper's counts of cells kept below 0.05 (69 of 97 ADN-HD, 789 of 1,602 PoSub-HD) imply. The claim was amended after a reader's answer to say only that the scores differ, and the criterion accepts the multipeak test in either direction; before the amendment the statement had ADN-HD scores higher, and the outcome was partially reproduced.

ed4cd-isomap-posub-central¶

In a joint Isomap embedding of tuning curve auto-correlograms, PoSub-HD cells lie nearer the centre of the PoSub-FS distribution than ADN-HD cells.

Isomap (12 neighbours, 2 dimensions) on the cross-validated auto-correlograms of FS, PoSub-HD and ADN-HD cells together; Euclidean distance of each HD cell to the mean FS position; Mann-Whitney U (criterion; Methods). Isomap from scikit-learn, not the MATLAB toolbox the paper used.

In [24]:
from sklearn.manifold import Isomap
ACA = posub.xval_autocorr(HA1, HA2)
Xac = np.c_[AC[:, fsm], AC[:, hdm], ACA].T
grp = np.r_[np.zeros(fsm.sum()), np.ones(hdm.sum()), 2 * np.ones(ACA.shape[1])]
okr = np.isfinite(Xac).all(1)
print("cells dropped for an undefined auto-correlogram (flat half):", int((~okr).sum()), "by group", np.bincount(grp[~okr].astype(int), minlength=3))
emb = Isomap(n_neighbors=12, n_components=2).fit_transform(Xac[okr]); g = grp[okr]
c = emb[g == 0].mean(0); dist = np.linalg.norm(emb - c, axis=1)
show(ranksum(dist[g == 1], dist[g == 2]), "distance to FS centre, PoSub-HD vs ADN-HD:")
print("paper: n = 1602 and 97, z = 4.26")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.5, 4))
for k, col in ((0, "tab:orange"), (1, "tab:purple"), (2, "magenta")):
    ax.scatter(*emb[g == k].T, s=3, c=col, label=["FS", "PoSub-HD", "ADN-HD"][k])
ax.legend(); plt.show()
print("embedding range", emb.min(0).round(2), emb.max(0).round(2))

fig4f-synaptic-weights-dispersed¶

Putative synaptic weights from PoSub-HD to PoSub-FS cells, estimated from spike train cross-correlograms, are heavy-tailed with an s.d. larger than their mean, in the range where simulations predict the radial symmetries of FS tuning.

Cross-correlograms over the whole recording in 0.2 ms bins, HD cell as reference; baseline from a partially hollowed Gaussian (cch_conv, 41 bins); the 99th percentile of the Poisson at the largest predicted count within 0 to 2 ms; at least two consecutive bins above it; peak at positive lag, latency above 0.5 ms, no peak at negative lag (criterion; GetSynapticPairs.m, FindSynapse_Exc, Figure_SynapticConnections.m). Weight strZ (peak minus prediction over the square root of the prediction); strR is a variant. CCG span plus or minus 50 ms (Methods) and plus or minus 25 ms (code).

In [25]:

    u = U[U.sess == si]
    hd_idx = np.where(u.hd.values)[0]; fs_idx = np.where(u.fs.values)[0]
    for i in hd_idx:
        for j in fs_idx:
            row = dict(subject=s["subject"], hd=i, fs=j)
            for span, nb in (("50", 500), ("25", 250)):
                c = posub.ccg_counts(s["spikes"][i], s["spikes"][j], nbins=nb)
                ln, zn, lp, zp, rp = posub.find_synapse_exc(c)
                row.update({f"lat_neg{span}": ln, f"z_neg{span}": zn, f"lat{span}": lp, f"z{span}": zp, f"r{span}": rp})

              f"s.d. {x.std():.2f}, CV {x.std() / x.mean():.2f}, skewness {stats.skew(x):.2f}, median {x.median():.2f}, max {x.max():.2f}")
    print("   connections per subject:", syn.groupby("subject").size().to_dict())

Result: reproduced. 1,176 putative HD-to-FS connections are found among 24,498 pairs (4.8%). Their strZ weights have mean 8.58 and s.d. 16.32 (CV 1.90) and skewness 9.34, heavy-tailed with an s.d. above the mean. The strR weights, a variant, have CV 0.71. The CCG spans of 50 and 25 ms give identical results, as they must: the test window (0 to 2 ms) and the baseline kernel (41 bins of 0.2 ms) never reach either edge, so the span variant does not test anything.

Optogenetic sessions¶

Sessions with TRN injections in VGAT-Cre mice and light over ADN: ArchT (virus field names ArchT and the thalamic reticular nucleus) and control (GFP only). Light ON is each 1 s pulse, OFF the 4 s before each onset (Methods; code offStart = 4). Cells are the square-epoch classes above, kept when their rates in ON, OFF and the square epoch (first to last tracked sample) all exceed 0.5 Hz (code, Figure_Optogenetics). Tuning curves in ON and OFF use no speed threshold (Methods): 1 degree bins with 3 degree smoothing for widths, 6 degree bins without smoothing for gain. The light pulses are decoded from the files' optogenetic series (helper light_pulses); their widths and intervals are printed, and they are checked against the figshare pulse table further below.

In [26]:
def opto_group(s):
    v = s["virus"]
    if "thalamic reticular" not in v:
        return None
    return "ArchT" if "ArchT" in v else ("control" if "GFP" in v else None)

def opto_rows(spikes, t, ang, on, base, hd, fs, **meta):
    """One row per unit of an optogenetic session: ON and OFF rates, light modulation, tuning
    curves in ON and OFF (no speed threshold), widths, gain factors. on is (240, 2) pulse
    times, base the square epoch (first to last tracked sample)."""
    off = np.c_[on[:, 0] - 4, on[:, 0]]
    m_on = posub.in_intervals(t, on) & np.isfinite(ang); m_off = posub.in_intervals(t, off) & np.isfinite(ang)
    h_on, _ = posub.tuning_curves(spikes, t, ang, m_on); h_off, _ = posub.tuning_curves(spikes, t, ang, m_off)
    g_on, _ = posub.tuning_curves(spikes, t, ang, m_on, nbins=60, sd=0); g_off, _ = posub.tuning_curves(spikes, t, ang, m_off, nbins=60, sd=0)
    w_on, _ = posub.peak_width(h_on); w_off, _ = posub.peak_width(h_off)
    rows = []
    for i, sp in enumerate(spikes):
        fr_on = np.array([((sp >= a) & (sp < b)).sum() / (b - a) for a, b in on])
        fr_off = np.array([((sp >= a) & (sp < b)).sum() / (b - a) for a, b in off])
        x, y = g_off[:, i], g_on[:, i]
        mx = x.max()
        ok = mx > 0 and x.std() > 0 and y.std() > 0
        r, p = stats.pearsonr(y, x) if ok else (np.nan, np.nan)
        slope, icpt = np.polyfit(x / mx, y / mx, 1) if ok else (np.nan, np.nan)
        rows.append(dict(meta, unit=i, hd=bool(hd[i]), fs=bool(fs[i]),
                         rate_on=fr_on.mean(), rate_off=fr_off.mean(), rate_base=((sp >= base[0]) & (sp < base[1])).sum() / (base[1] - base[0]),
                         p_light=stats.wilcoxon(fr_on, fr_off).pvalue if np.any(fr_on != fr_off) else 1.0,
                         r_tc=r, p_tc=p, mult=slope, add=icpt, w_on=w_on[i], w_off=w_off[i], g_off=x, g_on=y))
    return rows

OP = []
for si, s in enumerate(S):
    grp = opto_group(s)
    if grp is None or "pulses" not in s:
        continue
    u = U[U.sess == si]
    OP += opto_rows(s["spikes"], s["hd_t"], s["hd"], s["pulses"][:240], posub.tracked_epoch(s, "wake_square"),
                    u.hd.values, u.fs.values, subject=s["subject"], group=grp, sess=si)
OP = pd.DataFrame(OP)
OP["gd"] = (OP.rate_on > 0.5) & (OP.rate_off > 0.5) & (OP.rate_base > 0.5)
OP["mod"] = OP.rate_on / OP.rate_off
print("opto sessions:", OP.groupby("group").subject.unique().to_dict())
print("cells kept, by group and class:")
print(OP[OP.gd].groupby("group")[["hd", "fs"]].sum().to_string())
print("paper: ArchT 83 HD and 47 FS cells (5 mice); control 89 HD and 38 FS (3 mice)")
# the light pulses, decoded from the optogenetic series (helper light_pulses): count, width and
# interval between onsets, per session
for si in OP.sess.unique():
    pl = S[si]["pulses"]; w = pl[:, 1] - pl[:, 0]; gap = np.diff(pl[:, 0])
    print(f"{S[si]['subject']}: {len(pl)} pulses; width (s) min {w.min():.4f}, median {np.median(w):.4f}, max {w.max():.4f}; "
          f"onset interval (s) min {gap.min():.3f}, median {np.median(gap):.3f}, max {gap.max():.3f}; first onset {pl[0, 0]:.1f} s, "
          f"wake_opto epoch {[tuple(np.round(e, 1)) for e in S[si]['epochs'].get('wake_opto', [])]}")
# the optogenetic series itself (finding format_error): its length against the raw ElectricalSeries,
# its stated rate and unit, the channels read from it, and the values on each
for s in S:
    if "ogen_info" not in s:
        continue
    oi = s["ogen_info"]
    print(f"{s['subject']}: optogenetic_stim length {oi['length']:,} at {oi['rate']:.0f} Hz, unit {oi['unit']}; ElectricalSeries length {s['ephys_len']:,} "
          f"at {s['ephys_rate']:.0f} Hz ({s['ephys_len'] / s['ephys_rate']:.0f} s); ratio {oi['length'] / s['ephys_len']:.3f}; "
          f"channels {oi['channels']}, max per channel {oi['channel_max']}, min {oi['channel_min']}; light channel values {oi['light_values']}")
# the light times share the spike clock: the ON/OFF ratio with the true pulse times against the
# same ratio with every window moved 2.5 s later (ON in the middle of the 4 s gap, OFF across the
# pulse and the gap), over all kept cells
for grp in ("ArchT", "control"):
    d = OP[OP.gd & (OP.group == grp)]
    sh = []
    for si in d.sess.unique():
        s = S[si]; on = s["pulses"][:240] + 2.5; off = np.c_[on[:, 0] - 4, on[:, 0]]
        for i in d[d.sess == si].unit:
            sp = s["spikes"][i]
            ron = posub.in_intervals(sp, on).sum() / 240; roff = posub.in_intervals(sp, off).sum() / 960
            sh.append(ron / roff if roff > 0 else np.nan)
    print(f"{grp}: median ON/OFF rate ratio over {len(d)} kept cells {d['mod'].median():.3f}; with windows moved 2.5 s {np.nanmedian(sh):.3f}")

Result: reproduced. In the dandiset's two ArchT mice, FS and HD cells raise their rates with light (median ON/OFF ratio 1.33 and 1.46; signed-rank p = 8e-6 and 3e-9), above the three control mice (1.04 and 1.00) and in each ArchT mouse; the FS rise exceeds control (z = 5.41, p = 6e-8, n = 33 and 43; paper z = 4.99 for 47 and 38). The HD comparison with control is also significant here (z = 7.77, n = 62 and 92), where the paper's is not (z = 1.69 for 83 and 89); the criterion does not judge it. The dandiset holds 2 of the paper's 5 ArchT mice; the variant below adds the other three from figshare.

ed7gj-tuning-preserved¶

Thalamic disinhibition preserves the HD tuning of PoSub-HD and PoSub-FS cells.

fig5e-hd-multiplicative-fs-additive¶

Thalamic gain modulates PoSub-HD cell tuning multiplicatively and PoSub-FS cell tuning additively, so that FS cells receive thalamic input that is uniform across directions.

ON and OFF curves (6 degree bins, unsmoothed, no speed threshold) divided by the OFF maximum; linear fit of ON on OFF, slope multiplicative and intercept additive factor. ArchT cells are excluded (a) when both light modulation (Wilcoxon signed-rank of per-pulse ON against OFF rates) and the ON-OFF tuning correlation are not significant, (b) when either is not, (c) when the correlation is not (code).

Result: partially reproduced. Under all three exclusion readings HD multiplicative factors exceed FS ones (p from 1e-5 to 2e-8) and FS additive factors exceed HD ones (p from 5e-7 to 3e-10), HD multiplicative and FS additive factors exceed control (p below 3e-7 and 4e-4), and FS multiplicative factors do not differ from control (p 0.21 to 0.40). HD additive factors do not differ from control under readings (a) and (c) (p = 0.19) but do under reading (b) (p = 0.015), which excludes 31 of 62 HD cells; the criterion asks for every reading. The paper excluded 1 FS cell and no other cell, as readings (a) and (c) do here (0 HD and 0 or 1 FS cells); whether the claims file should keep reading (b) is asked of a reader (questions/000939.yaml).

ed8cd-multiplicative-detectable¶

Simulations of noisy gain on real FS tuning curves show that multiplicative gain would be detectable at the FS cells' tuning correlations, and the FS data are best explained by additive gain.

As Figure_GainSimulation.m: OFF curves (6 degree bins, unsmoothed) of all kept cells; for ArchT cells the simulated ON curve is (OFF + a x max(OFF)) x m with, per cell, no gain (m = 1, a = 0), multiplicative gain (m drawn from N(1.2, 0.33), a = 0) or additive gain (m = 1, a drawn from N(0.2, 0.1)); control cells get ON = OFF. Gaussian noise is added to OFF and ON independently, and factors are computed as for the data. The noise is read two ways: titrated, as the Methods and the criterion say, so that the no-gain simulation's median ON-OFF correlation matches the observed one (the main reading, second block below); and fixed at 1.8 x 1.8 Hz, as the code's noiseMag sets it (first block, a variant). The simulated ArchT FS factors are compared with the control group's, read two ways: the simulated control cells (ON = OFF plus noise, as Figure_GainSimulation.m builds them) and the recorded control factors. The code's choice of FS cells (ArchT cells with a significant tuning correlation, reading (c)) is used. Seeds fixed; the titrated simulation is repeated over 50 seeds.

In [30]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(8)
fs_a = OP[OP.gd & OP.fs & (OP.group == "ArchT") & (OP.p_tc < 0.05)]
fs_c = OP[OP.gd & OP.fs & (OP.group == "control")]
def sim_factors(rows, mult, add, noise=1.8 * 1.8):
    out = []
    for _, r in rows.iterrows():
        x = r.g_off
        m = rng.normal(*mult) if mult else 1.0
        a = rng.normal(*add) if add else 0.0
        y = (x + a * x.max()) * m
        xo = x + rng.normal(0, noise, len(x)); yo = y + rng.normal(0, noise, len(x))
        mx = xo.max()
        sl, ic = np.polyfit(xo / mx, yo / mx, 1)
        out.append((sl, ic, np.corrcoef(xo, yo)[0, 1]))
    return np.array(out)
ctrl = sim_factors(fs_c, None, None)
print(f"observed ON-OFF correlation of ArchT FS cells: median {fs_a.r_tc.median():.3f}; simulated control: median {np.median(ctrl[:, 2]):.3f}")
for name, mult, add in (("no gain", None, None), ("multiplicative", (1.2, 0.33), None), ("additive", None, (0.2, 0.1))):
    sim = sim_factors(fs_a, mult, add)
    rm_, ra_ = ranksum(sim[:, 0], ctrl[:, 0]), ranksum(sim[:, 1], ctrl[:, 1])
    print(f"{name}: simulated correlation median {np.median(sim[:, 2]):.3f}; multiplicative vs control z = {rm_['z']:.2f}, p = {rm_['p']:.3g} "
          f"(medians {rm_['median_a']:.3f}, {rm_['median_b']:.3f}); additive vs control z = {ra_['z']:.2f}, p = {ra_['p']:.3g} "
          f"(medians {ra_['median_a']:.3f}, {ra_['median_b']:.3f})")
    vm, va = ranksum(sim[:, 0], fs_c.mult), ranksum(sim[:, 1], fs_c["add"])
    print(f"   variant, against the recorded control FS factors: multiplicative p = {vm['p']:.3g}, additive p = {va['p']:.3g}")
r1, r2 = ranksum(fs_a.mult, fs_c.mult), ranksum(fs_a["add"], fs_c["add"])
print(f"data: FS multiplicative vs control p = {r1['p']:.3g}, additive vs control p = {r2['p']:.3g}")
# Methods reading: the noise is titrated until the simulated correlations resemble the observed
# ones. Noise s.d. (Hz) chosen on a grid so that the no-gain simulation's median ON-OFF
# correlation is closest to the observed median of the ArchT FS cells.
grid = np.arange(1.0, 12.01, 0.25)
med = []
for nz in grid:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(80)
    med.append(np.median(sim_factors(fs_a, None, None, noise=nz)[:, 2]))
nz = grid[np.argmin(np.abs(np.array(med) - fs_a.r_tc.median()))]
print(f"titrated noise s.d. {nz:.2f} Hz (no-gain median r {med[int(np.argmin(np.abs(np.array(med) - fs_a.r_tc.median())))]:.3f}, observed {fs_a.r_tc.median():.3f})")
rng = np.random.default_rng(81)
ctrl_t = sim_factors(fs_c, None, None, noise=nz)
for name, mult, add in (("no gain", None, None), ("multiplicative", (1.2, 0.33), None), ("additive", None, (0.2, 0.1))):
    sim = sim_factors(fs_a, mult, add, noise=nz)
    rm_, ra_ = ranksum(sim[:, 0], ctrl_t[:, 0]), ranksum(sim[:, 1], ctrl_t[:, 1])
    vm, va = ranksum(sim[:, 0], fs_c.mult), ranksum(sim[:, 1], fs_c["add"])
    print(f"titrated, {name}: median r {np.median(sim[:, 2]):.3f}; vs simulated control: multiplicative p = {rm_['p']:.3g}, additive p = {ra_['p']:.3g}; "
          f"vs recorded control: multiplicative p = {vm['p']:.3g}, additive p = {va['p']:.3g}")
# how often the criterion holds over 50 seeds (titrated noise, simulated control)
hits = []
for seed in range(50):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1000 + seed)
    c_ = sim_factors(fs_c, None, None, noise=nz); mu_ = sim_factors(fs_a, (1.2, 0.33), None, noise=nz); ad_ = sim_factors(fs_a, None, (0.2, 0.1), noise=nz)
    hits.append((ranksum(mu_[:, 0], c_[:, 0])["p"] < 0.05, ranksum(ad_[:, 1], c_[:, 1])["p"] < 0.05, ranksum(ad_[:, 0], c_[:, 0])["p"] >= 0.05))
hits = np.array(hits)
print("over 50 seeds: multiplicative detected", hits[:, 0].mean(), "; additive detected", hits[:, 1].mean(),
      "; additive simulation without a multiplicative difference", hits[:, 2].mean(), "; all three", hits.all(1).mean())

Result: reproduced. The criterion asks for noise titrated to the observed correlations, so the code's fixed noise (3.24 Hz) is a variant and not a reading of the criterion. With the noise titrated (4.25 Hz; no-gain median r 0.731 against the observed 0.730) and the simulated control cells, as Figure_GainSimulation.m builds them, simulated multiplicative gain is detected (p = 0.022) and simulated additive gain shows the data's pattern (additive p = 8e-5, multiplicative p = 0.13), as in the data (p = 3e-4 and 0.27); over 50 seeds all three hold in 80% of runs. The titration used seed 80; in the seed-81 run the simulated median correlations are 0.69 to 0.71, slightly below the observed 0.73. Against the recorded control factors the titrated additive simulation also changes the multiplicative factor (p = 0.0008), but this comparison fails its own check: the titrated no-gain simulation already differs from the recorded control (multiplicative p = 0.0026, additive p = 0.039), so it cannot tell one gain type from another. Under the one comparison that passes the no-gain check the criterion holds. The outcome was partially reproduced until round 3 of verification, as it counted the fixed-noise readings, which the criterion does not call for; the verifier agreed with the change to reproduced. Variant with the code's fixed noise (simulated correlations about 0.82, above the observed 0.73): against the simulated control the additive simulation changes the multiplicative factor (p = 0.008), and against the recorded control the multiplicative simulation is not detected (p = 0.80).

ADN optogenetic sessions (figshare, claims with data elsewhere)¶

The ADN recordings with light over ADN are not in the dandiset. The claims file names their source, figshare doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.24921252 version 3, Dataset_6.tar.gz, streamed here. The same tarball holds the PoSub ArchT sessions of three mice (A1801, A1804, A1806) that the dandiset lacks; the PoSub claims are judged on the dandiset, and these mice are added in a variant after the ADN claims. ON is each of the first 240 pulses (Opto_TS.csv), OFF the 4 s before each onset; cells are kept with rates above 0.5 Hz in ON, OFF and the square epoch (code, Figure_Optogenetics). ADN-HD cells as GetCellTypes_ADN (rate above 0.5 Hz, HD information at least 0.2 bits per spike in the square epoch at speed above 2 cm/s); non-HD cells the others above 0.5 Hz.

print("sessions in Dataset_6:", [(o["session"], "ADN" if o["adn"].any() else "PoSub", {1: "ArchT", 2: "control"}.get(o.get("group")), len(o["spikes"])) for o in O])

print("PoSub opto sessions in Dataset_6 whose mouse is not in the dandiset:",
      [o["session"] for o in O if not o["adn"].any() and o["session"].split("-")[0] not in dandi_subjects])
AO = []
for o in O:
    if not o["adn"].any():
        continue
    o = dict(o); o["eps"] = dict(o["eps"]); o["eps"].setdefault("wake1Ep", o["eps"]["wakeEp"])
    tun = posub.adn_tuning(o)
    hd = (tun["rate"] > 0.5) & (tun["info"] >= 0.2)
    nhd = (tun["rate"] > 0.5) & (tun["info"] < 0.2)
    on = o["pulses"][:240, :2]; off = np.c_[on[:, 0] - 4, on[:, 0]]
    t, ang = o["hd_t"], o["hd"]
    m_on = posub.in_intervals(t, on) & np.isfinite(ang); m_off = posub.in_intervals(t, off) & np.isfinite(ang)
    h_on, _ = posub.tuning_curves(o["spikes"], t, ang, m_on); h_off, _ = posub.tuning_curves(o["spikes"], t, ang, m_off)
    g_on, _ = posub.tuning_curves(o["spikes"], t, ang, m_on, nbins=60, sd=0); g_off, _ = posub.tuning_curves(o["spikes"], t, ang, m_off, nbins=60, sd=0)
    w_on, _ = posub.peak_width(h_on); w_off, _ = posub.peak_width(h_off)
    ep = o["eps"]["wakeEp"]; tt = t[posub.in_intervals(t, ep) & np.isfinite(ang)]; ba, bb = tt[0], tt[-1]
    for i, sp in enumerate(o["spikes"]):
        fr_on = np.array([((sp >= a) & (sp < b)).sum() / (b - a) for a, b in on])
        fr_off = np.array([((sp >= a) & (sp < b)).sum() / (b - a) for a, b in off])
        x, y = g_off[:, i], g_on[:, i]; mx = x.max()
        ok = mx > 0 and x.std() > 0 and y.std() > 0
        r, p = stats.pearsonr(y, x) if ok else (np.nan, np.nan)
        slope, icpt = np.polyfit(x / mx, y / mx, 1) if ok else (np.nan, np.nan)
        AO.append(dict(session=o["session"], mouse=o["session"].split("-")[0], hd=bool(hd[i]), nhd=bool(nhd[i]), file_hd=bool(o["file_hd"][i]),
                       rate_on=fr_on.mean(), rate_off=fr_off.mean(), rate_base=((sp >= ba) & (sp < bb)).sum() / (bb - ba),
                       p_light=stats.wilcoxon(fr_on, fr_off).pvalue if np.any(fr_on != fr_off) else 1.0, r_tc=r, p_tc=p,
                       mult=slope, add=icpt, w_on=w_on[i], w_off=w_off[i]))
AO = pd.DataFrame(AO)
AO["gd"] = (AO.rate_on > 0.5) & (AO.rate_off > 0.5) & (AO.rate_base > 0.5)
AO["mod"] = AO.rate_on / AO.rate_off
print("ADN opto sessions:", AO.session.nunique(), "mice:", AO.mouse.nunique(), "; units", len(AO), "; kept", int(AO.gd.sum()),
      "; ADN-HD kept", int((AO.gd & AO.hd).sum()), "; non-HD kept", int((AO.gd & AO.nhd).sum()),
      "; agreement of recomputed HD with the files' CellTypes", (AO.hd == AO.file_hd).mean().round(3))

ed7-adn-disinhibition¶

Light over ADN in VGAT-Cre mice with ArchT in TRN raises the firing of ADN-HD cells but not of non-HD thalamic cells, without broadening ADN-HD tuning curves.

Result: reproduced. In the figshare ADN sessions (10 sessions, 3 mice, 127 cells kept, 53 ADN-HD), light raises ADN-HD rates more than non-HD rates (median ON/OFF ratio 1.54 against 1.06, z = 6.85, p = 8e-12; paper z = 6.57), non-HD rates do not change significantly (p = 0.13), and ADN-HD widths do not change (62 against 58 degrees, signed-rank p = 0.61; rank-sum p = 0.80).

PoSub ArchT mice from figshare Dataset_6 (variant for fig5b, ed7gj, fig5e and ed8cd)¶

The dandiset holds 2 of the paper's 5 ArchT mice of the PoSub optogenetic experiment. The other three (A1801, A1804 and A1806, two sessions each) are in figshare Dataset_6, streamed above for the ADN claims. The four PoSub optogenetic claims are judged on the dandiset (the claims file gives them data: dataset); this variant adds the three figshare mice to the ArchT group, to show how the paper's sample size bears on the results. Cell classes for the figshare sessions are recomputed as for the dandiset (Methods), from the files' trough-to-peak and Velocity series; the files' own CellTypes are printed beside them. The dandiset's decoded light pulses are checked against the figshare pulse table (Opto_TS.csv) for the five mice in both.

# PoSub ArchT sessions of Dataset_6 whose mice are not in the dandiset; classes recomputed as for

OPF, cls_rows = [], []
for o in O:
    if o["adn"].any() or o.get("group") != 1 or o["session"].split("-")[0] in dandi_subjects:
        continue
    tun = posub.adn_tuning(o)
    ttp = o["mat"]["tr2pk"].ravel().astype(float)
    gd = (tun["rate"] >= posub.RATE_MIN) & np.isfinite(ttp)
    ex = gd & (ttp > posub.TTP_CUT) & (tun["rate"] < posub.FS_RATE)
    fs = gd & (ttp < posub.TTP_CUT) & (tun["rate"] > posub.FS_RATE)
    hd = ex & (tun["info"] > posub.HD_INFO_TH)
    cls_rows.append(dict(session=o["session"], units=len(o["spikes"]), hd=int(hd.sum()), fs=int(fs.sum()),
                         file_hd=int(o["file_types"]["hd"].sum()), file_fs=int(o["file_types"]["fs"].sum()),
                         agree_hd=(hd == o["file_types"]["hd"]).mean().round(3), agree_fs=(fs == o["file_types"]["fs"]).mean().round(3)))
    t, ang = o["hd_t"], o["hd"]
    ep = o["eps"]["wakeEp"]; tt = t[posub.in_intervals(t, ep) & np.isfinite(ang)]
    OPF += opto_rows(o["spikes"], t, ang, o["pulses"][:240, :2], (tt[0], tt[-1]), hd, fs,

With the three figshare ArchT mice added (6 sessions; 102 HD and 50 FS ArchT cells kept from 5 mice, paper 83 and 47; the recomputed classes agree with the files' CellTypes for 69 to 100% of units per session for HD), the four claims come out as on the dandiset alone. fig5b: FS ArchT against control z = 5.60, p = 2e-8, ArchT medians 1.29 (FS) and 1.32 (HD) above the control medians, though one mouse (A1804) has medians below 1 (0.94 and 0.93). ed7gj: HD widths p = 0.24 (signed-rank), FS correlation p = 0.95. fig5e: every condition holds under readings (a) and (c) (HD additive against control p = 0.11), and under (b), which excludes 52 HD cells, HD additive against control gives p = 0.016. ed8cd: titrated noise (4.00 Hz) with the simulated control detects multiplicative gain (p = 0.019) and the additive simulation shows the data's pattern (additive p = 3e-7, multiplicative p = 0.38); against the recorded control the additive simulation changes the multiplicative factor (p = 7e-5). The dandiset's decoded light pulses match the figshare pulse table within 0.1 ms in all five PoSub opto mice in both.

fig6c-coupling-preserved-wake-rem¶

GLM cross-coupling of PoSub-HD pairs, PoSub-FS pairs and PoSub-HD to PoSub-FS pairs is preserved between wakefulness and REM sleep, less for FS pairs than for HD pairs.

Sessions with at least 100 s of REM (Methods). As GetGLM_Forward.m and GetGLM_Reverse.m: spike counts of every unit in 100 ms bins over the whole recording, smoothed with a Gaussian of 1 bin s.d.; the population rate (sum over all units) smoothed alike and z-scored; cell B's train z-scored; Poisson GLM of cell A's smoothed train on the population rate and cell B, within WAKE (square epoch) or REM; the coefficient on B at lag 0, averaged with that of the reversed pair. Cells as Figure_GLMRemWake.m selects them (ixHd = isHd & isGd, ixFs = isFs & isGd: the HD and FS classes, with no rate condition in WAKE or REM). REM is the scored REM inside the home-cage epochs (data check). Only lag 0 is fitted (the claim uses lag 0).

Pairs with fit warnings are removed (criterion). Figure_GLMRemWake.m removes a pair when glmfit raised any warning (lastwarn) in any of its fits: WAKE or REM, either order, any of the 201 lags. The fits here mirror glmfit's iteratively reweighted least squares (helper glmfit_poisson_batch) and flag its two warnings for a Poisson fit: weights ill-conditioned (a weight below eps^(2/3) of the largest at any iteration) and the iteration limit; a singular system is flagged too. MATLAB is not run, so that this mirror flags the pairs glmfit would is an assumption. Shown as variants: the round-1 rule (the final fitted means spanning more than eps^(-4/3), or no convergence), no removal, and the round-1 selection of cells above 1 Hz in both WAKE and REM, which came from a sanity-check block of GetGLM_Forward.m that runs after its return statement. The flagged pairs are described (coefficients and REM rates).

from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
glm_rows = []
t_glm = time.time()
EPS43 = (4 / 3) * np.log(np.finfo(float).eps)
for si, s in enumerate(S):
    remiv = s["sleep"].get("rem", np.zeros((0, 2)))
    if (remiv[:, 1] - remiv[:, 0]).sum() < 100:
        continue
    u = U[U.sess == si]
    tmax = max(b for v in s["epochs"].values() for a, b in v)
    edges = np.arange(0, tmax + 0.1, 0.1); cen = edges[:-1] + 0.05
    Q = gaussian_filter1d(posub.bin_counts(s["spikes"], edges), 1, axis=0)
    mua = Q.sum(1); mua = (mua - mua.mean()) / mua.std()
    Qz = (Q - Q.mean(0)) / Q.std(0)
    wa, wb = s["epochs"]["wake_square"][0]
    states = {"WAKE": (cen >= wa) & (cen < wb), "REM": posub.in_intervals(cen, remiv)}
    rate_w = np.array([((sp >= wa) & (sp < wb)).sum() / (wb - wa) for sp in s["spikes"]])
    rem_dur = (remiv[:, 1] - remiv[:, 0]).sum()
    rate_r = np.array([posub.in_intervals(sp, remiv).sum() / rem_dur for sp in s["spikes"]])
    # the code's selection (Figure_GLMRemWake.m: ixHd = isHd & isGd, ixFs = isFs & isGd), with no
    # rate condition in WAKE or REM; the 1 Hz condition is a variant below
    cells = np.where((u.hd | u.fs).values)[0]
    res = {}
    for st, msk in states.items():
        Qm, mm, Zm = Q[msk], mua[msk], Qz[msk]
        def fit(a):
            others = np.array([c for c in cells if c != a])
            b, bad, lim = posub.glmfit_poisson_batch(Qm[:, a], mm, Zm[:, others])
            with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
                eta = b[0] + np.outer(mm, b[1]) + Zm[:, others] * b[2]
                lr = eta.min(0) - eta.max(0)  # log of the smallest over the largest fitted mean
            return b[2], bad, lim, ~(lr > EPS43)
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
            out = list(ex.map(fit, cells))
        B = np.full((len(cells), len(cells)), np.nan); W = np.zeros_like(B, bool); L = W.copy(); F = W.copy()
        for ia, (b2, bad, lim, fin) in enumerate(out):
            col = [k for k in range(len(cells)) if k != ia]
            B[ia, col] = b2; W[ia, col] = bad; L[ia, col] = lim; F[ia, col] = fin
        res[st] = (B, W, L, F)
    cls = np.where(u.hd.values[cells], "HD", "FS")
    tcr = posub.zero_lag_r(np.repeat(TC[si]["sq3"][:, cells], len(cells), 1), np.tile(TC[si]["sq3"][:, cells], (1, len(cells)))).reshape(len(cells), len(cells))
    for i in range(len(cells)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(cells)):
            pair = "-".join(sorted([cls[i], cls[j]], key=lambda c: c != "HD"))
            f = lambda st, k: bool(res[st][k][i, j] or res[st][k][j, i])
            glm_rows.append(dict(subject=s["subject"], sess=si, ci=int(cells[i]), cj=int(cells[j]), pair=pair,
                                 wake=(res["WAKE"][0][i, j] + res["WAKE"][0][j, i]) / 2, rem=(res["REM"][0][i, j] + res["REM"][0][j, i]) / 2,
                                 tc_r=tcr[i, j], bad_scale=f("WAKE", 1) or f("REM", 1), iter_lim=f("WAKE", 2) or f("REM", 2),
                                 final_ratio=f("WAKE", 3) or f("REM", 3),
                                 rate_rem_min=min(rate_r[cells[i]], rate_r[cells[j]]), rate_wake_min=min(rate_w[cells[i]], rate_w[cells[j]])))

# Warnings at other lags. GetGLM_Forward.m fits every pair at 201 lags (the target cell's smoothed
# counts circshifted by -100 to 100 bins of 0.1 s over the whole recording, then restricted to the
# state), and Figure_GLMRemWake.m removes a pair with a warning at any lag. Only lag 0 is fitted
# above. Here every third session of the 27 is also fitted at lags of -10, -1, 1 and 10 s (four of
# the 200 other lags, chosen for time), and the pairs with a warning at any of these lags are
# removed as well, to see how many more pairs the code's rule would remove and how the
# correlations of those sessions change.
t_lag = time.time()
lag_sess = sorted(GL.sess.unique())[::3]
LAGS = (-100, -10, 10, 100)
lag_warn = {lg: set() for lg in LAGS}
for si in lag_sess:
    s = S[si]
    remiv = s["sleep"]["rem"]
    tmax = max(b for v in s["epochs"].values() for a, b in v)
    edges = np.arange(0, tmax + 0.1, 0.1); cen = edges[:-1] + 0.05
    Q = gaussian_filter1d(posub.bin_counts(s["spikes"], edges), 1, axis=0)
    mua = Q.sum(1); mua = (mua - mua.mean()) / mua.std()
    Qz = (Q - Q.mean(0)) / Q.std(0)
    wa, wb = s["epochs"]["wake_square"][0]
    states = {"WAKE": (cen >= wa) & (cen < wb), "REM": posub.in_intervals(cen, remiv)}
    u = U[U.sess == si]
    cells = np.where((u.hd | u.fs).values)[0]
    for lg in LAGS:
        Ql = np.roll(Q, lg, axis=0)  # MATLAB's circshift(dQ, lag)
        for st, msk in states.items():
            Qm, mm, Zm = Ql[msk], mua[msk], Qz[msk]
            def fit_lag(a):
                others = np.array([c for c in cells if c != a])
                b, bad, lim = posub.glmfit_poisson_batch(Qm[:, a], mm, Zm[:, others])
                w = bad | lim | ~np.isfinite(b).all(0)
                return {(si, int(min(a, o)), int(max(a, o))) for o in others[w]}
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
                for w in ex.map(fit_lag, cells):
                    lag_warn[lg] |= w
print(f"fitted at {len(LAGS)} more lags in {len(lag_sess)} sessions ({[S[i]['subject'] for i in lag_sess]}) in {time.time() - t_lag:.0f} s")
GLs = GL[GL.sess.isin(lag_sess)].copy()
key = list(zip(GLs.sess, GLs.ci, GLs.cj))
for lg in LAGS:
    GLs[f"warn_{lg}"] = [k in lag_warn[lg] for k in key]
GLs["warn_any"] = GLs.warn | GLs[[f"warn_{lg}" for lg in LAGS]].any(axis=1)
for p_ in ("HD-HD", "FS-FS", "HD-FS"):
    d = GLs[GLs.pair == p_]
    print(f"{p_}: {len(d)} pairs in these sessions; warning at lag 0 {int(d.warn.sum())}; "
          + "; ".join(f"at {lg / 10:+.0f} s {int(d[f'warn_{lg}'].sum())}" for lg in LAGS)
          + f"; at any of the five {int(d.warn_any.sum())}, of which not at lag 0 {int((d.warn_any & ~d.warn).sum())}")
print("WAKE against REM coupling in these sessions:")
corr_table(GLs[~GLs.warn], "warnings at lag 0 removed (as the main result)")
corr_table(GLs[~GLs.warn_any], "warnings at any of the five lags removed")

Result: reproduced (resting on an assumption). With the code's cell selection (HD and FS cells, no rate condition), 27 sessions give 34,611 HD-HD, 2,683 FS-FS and 19,602 HD-FS pairs after the removal of fits with glmfit's warnings (paper 34,270, 2,492 and 18,992 in Extended Data Fig. 9d). WAKE and REM coupling coefficients are correlated for HD-HD pairs (r = 0.641), FS-FS pairs (r = 0.364, p = 1e-84) and HD-FS pairs (r = 0.359), all positive with p < 0.05, and FS-FS is below HD-HD; the Spearman correlations are 0.762, 0.417 and 0.514. The glmfit mirror flags 1,795 HD-HD pairs (4.9%), 24 HD-FS and no FS-FS pairs; the round-1 rule flags the same pairs (agreement 1.0). The flagged HD-HD fits are divergent (median |coupling| 2.77 in WAKE, up to 3e73, against 0.28 in kept pairs), and with them kept the pooled HD-HD Pearson r is 0.000 while the Spearman r is 0.759, so the outcome rests on the assumption that the mirror flags the pairs glmfit would. The round-1 selection of cells above 1 Hz in WAKE and REM gives r = 0.698, 0.380 and 0.425. Warnings at other lags (the code removes a pair with a warning at any of 201 lags) were checked in 9 of the 27 sessions at -10, -1, 1 and 10 s: they flag 60 more HD-HD pairs of 10,507 (0.6%; 417 at lag 0) and no more FS-FS or HD-FS pairs, and removing them moves the HD-HD r of those sessions from 0.638 to 0.647, FS-FS and HD-FS unchanged (0.282 and 0.479).

ed9d-coupling-follows-tuning¶

The polarity of the GLM coupling within a pair depends on the similarity of the two cells' HD tuning, during both WAKE and REM.

Pearson correlation across pairs between the zero-lag correlation of the two cells' square tuning curves and the lag-0 coupling, for HD-FS and FS-FS pairs, in WAKE and in REM (criterion; code Figure_GLMRemWake).
