fig7b-wake-isomap-tuning¶

HD tuning curves of PoSub-HD and PoSub-FS cells computed from the virtual HD of the WAKE ring manifold are equivalent to those computed from the real HD.

Methods and GetIsomap_WAKE.m: HD cell spikes over the whole square epoch in 200 ms bins, smoothed with 400 ms s.d., square root; Isomap with 12 neighbours and 3 dimensions; virtual HD from the first two dimensions, its direction by the smaller circular variance of its difference from real HD, its origin by the mean offset of maximum cross-correlation between real and virtual curves over HD cells. Curves in 1 degree bins, 3 degree smoothing, from all times of the epoch (code); real HD taken at each bin centre. Control: the virtual HD reversed in time. Isomap is fitted on at most 4,000 vectors per session (helper; assumption, for time).

In [38]:
ISO = {}
iso_rows = []
for si, s in enumerate(S):
    u = U[U.sess == si]
    a, b = s["epochs"]["wake_square"][0]
    edges = np.arange(a, b, 0.2); cen = edges[:-1] + 0.1
    t = s["hd_t"]
    j = np.clip(np.searchsorted(t, cen), 1, len(t) - 1); j = np.where(np.abs(t[j - 1] - cen) < np.abs(t[j] - cen), j - 1, j)
    real = np.where(np.abs(t[j] - cen) < 0.05, s["hd"][j], np.nan)
    hd_idx = np.where(u.hd.values)[0]
    X = posub.pop_vectors([s["spikes"][i] for i in hd_idx], edges)
    emb = posub.isomap_embed(X, 3, seed=700 + si)
    v = posub.virtual_hd(emb, real)
    allm = np.ones(len(cen), bool)
    h_real = posub.binned_tuning(s["spikes"], edges, real, allm)
    h_vir = posub.binned_tuning(s["spikes"], edges, v, allm)
    lag = posub.circ_xcorr_lag(h_real[:, hd_idx], h_vir[:, hd_idx])
    off = int(np.round(np.rad2deg(stats.circmean(np.deg2rad(lag))))) % 360
    v = v - np.deg2rad(off)  # the virtual curve rolled back by off bins to match the real one
    h_vir = posub.binned_tuning(s["spikes"], edges, v, allm)
    h_rev = posub.binned_tuning(s["spikes"], edges, v[::-1].copy(), allm)
    r = posub.zero_lag_r(h_real, h_vir); rc = posub.zero_lag_r(h_real, h_rev)
    rad = np.linalg.norm(emb[:, :2] - emb[:, :2].mean(0), axis=1)
    ISO[si] = dict(emb=emb, v=v, real=real, edges=edges, rad=rad)
    for i in np.where((u.hd | u.fs).values)[0]:
        iso_rows.append(dict(subject=s["subject"], cls="HD" if u.hd.values[i] else "FS", r=r[i], r_rev=rc[i]))
IR = pd.DataFrame(iso_rows)
for cls in ("HD", "FS"):
    d = IR[IR.cls == cls]
    show(signrank(d.r, d.r_rev), f"{cls}: real vs virtual curve correlation, against reversed control:")
print("paper: HD n = 1602, z = 34.7; FS n = 427, z = 17.9")
print("per session median r (HD, FS):", IR.groupby(["subject", "cls"]).r.median().unstack().round(2).T.to_string())
print(f"Isomap done at {time.time() - T0:.0f} s")

ed10b-ring-topology¶

Population vectors of PoSub-HD cells lie on a ring during WAKE, farther from the centre of the manifold than shuffled vectors, and the ring has the same radius during REM.

Distance of each point to the centre of the first two Isomap dimensions, normalized to the mean distance of the real projection. Shuffle: each cell's binned train shifted circularly by a random number of bins, then embedded the same way. Real against shuffled mean distance, Wilcoxon signed-rank across sessions. REM against WAKE: the joint embedding below (WAKE vectors subsampled to the number of REM vectors), mean distance per session in each state, Wilcoxon signed-rank (a claim of absence, judged at p < 0.05).

In [39]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(10)
ring = []
for si, s in enumerate(S):
    u = U[U.sess == si]; hd_idx = np.where(u.hd.values)[0]
    e = ISO[si]["edges"]
    C = posub.bin_counts([s["spikes"][i] for i in hd_idx], e)
    C = np.stack([np.roll(C[:, k], rng.integers(len(C))) for k in range(C.shape[1])], 1)
    Xs = np.sqrt(gaussian_filter1d(C, 2, axis=0))
    es = posub.isomap_embed(Xs, 3, seed=900 + si)
    rr = ISO[si]["rad"]; rs = np.linalg.norm(es[:, :2] - es[:, :2].mean(0), axis=1)
    ring.append(dict(subject=s["subject"], real=1.0, shuffled=rs.mean() / rr.mean(), real_cv=rr.std() / rr.mean(), shuffled_cv=rs.std() / rs.mean()))
ring = pd.DataFrame(ring)
print(ring.round(3).to_string())
show(signrank(ring.real, ring.shuffled), "mean normalized distance, real (1 by construction) vs shuffled:")

fig7d-rem-isomap-tuning¶

During REM sleep the HD tuning of PoSub-HD and PoSub-FS cells can be estimated from the virtual HD of the ring manifold alone and matches their WAKE tuning.

Sessions with at least 100 s of REM (Methods). HD-cell population vectors (200 ms, 400 ms s.d., square root) in REM and in the square epoch; WAKE vectors subsampled at random to the number of REM vectors; Isomap (12 neighbours, 3 dimensions) on both together; virtual HD set in direction and origin from the WAKE vectors' real HD. Curves in 6 degree bins with 6 degree smoothing. Cells with REM rate above 0.5 Hz (HD) or 10 Hz (FS). WAKE curve read (i) as the WAKE Isomap curve and (ii) as the real-HD WAKE curve; control, the REM curve from the REM virtual HD reversed in time.

In [40]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
rem_rows, rad_rows = [], []
for si, s in enumerate(S):
    remiv = s["sleep"].get("rem", np.zeros((0, 2)))
    if (remiv[:, 1] - remiv[:, 0]).sum() < 100:
        continue
    u = U[U.sess == si]; hd_idx = np.where(u.hd.values)[0]
    tmax = max(b for v in s["epochs"].values() for a, b in v)
    edges = np.arange(0, tmax, 0.2); cen = edges[:-1] + 0.1
    in_rem = posub.in_intervals(cen, remiv)
    a, b = s["epochs"]["wake_square"][0]
    in_wk = (cen >= a) & (cen < b)
    wk_idx = np.sort(rng.choice(np.where(in_wk)[0], in_rem.sum(), replace=False))
    rem_idx = np.where(in_rem)[0]
    X = posub.pop_vectors([s["spikes"][i] for i in hd_idx], edges)
    sel = np.r_[wk_idx, rem_idx]
    emb = posub.isomap_embed(X[sel], 3, seed=1100 + si)
    t = s["hd_t"]
    j = np.clip(np.searchsorted(t, cen[sel]), 1, len(t) - 1); j = np.where(np.abs(t[j - 1] - cen[sel]) < np.abs(t[j] - cen[sel]), j - 1, j)
    real = np.where(np.abs(t[j] - cen[sel]) < 0.05, s["hd"][j], np.nan)
    nw = len(wk_idx); real[nw:] = np.nan
    v = posub.virtual_hd(emb, real)  # direction from the WAKE vectors (REM real HD is NaN)
    ang_full = np.full(len(cen), np.nan); ang_full[sel] = v
    real_full = np.full(len(cen), np.nan); real_full[sel[:nw]] = real[:nw]
    mw = np.zeros(len(cen), bool); mw[wk_idx] = True
    mr = np.zeros(len(cen), bool); mr[rem_idx] = True
    kw = dict(nbins=60, sd=1)
    hw_real = posub.binned_tuning(s["spikes"], edges, real_full, mw, **kw)
    hw_vir = posub.binned_tuning(s["spikes"], edges, ang_full, mw, **kw)
    lag = posub.circ_xcorr_lag(hw_real[:, hd_idx], hw_vir[:, hd_idx])
    off = stats.circmean(np.deg2rad(lag * 6))
    ang_full = ang_full - off
    hw_vir = posub.binned_tuning(s["spikes"], edges, ang_full, mw, **kw)
    hr_vir = posub.binned_tuning(s["spikes"], edges, ang_full, mr, **kw)
    rev = ang_full.copy(); rev[rem_idx] = ang_full[rem_idx][::-1]
    hr_rev = posub.binned_tuning(s["spikes"], edges, rev, mr, **kw)
    rem_dur = (remiv[:, 1] - remiv[:, 0]).sum()
    rate_rem = np.array([posub.in_intervals(sp, remiv).sum() / rem_dur for sp in s["spikes"]])
    ri = posub.zero_lag_r(hw_vir, hr_vir); rii = posub.zero_lag_r(hw_real, hr_vir)
    ci = posub.zero_lag_r(hw_vir, hr_rev); cii = posub.zero_lag_r(hw_real, hr_rev)
    for i in range(len(u)):
        cls = "HD" if u.hd.values[i] and rate_rem[i] > 0.5 else ("FS" if u.fs.values[i] and rate_rem[i] > 10 else None)
        if cls:
            rem_rows.append(dict(subject=s["subject"], cls=cls, r_iso=ri[i], r_real=rii[i], c_iso=ci[i], c_real=cii[i]))
    rad = np.linalg.norm(emb[:, :2] - emb[:, :2].mean(0), axis=1); rad = rad / rad[:nw].mean()
    wv = posub.zero_lag_r(hw_real[:, hd_idx], hw_vir[:, hd_idx])
    rad_rows.append(dict(subject=s["subject"], rem_s=round(rem_dur), n_vectors=int(in_rem.sum()), wake=rad[:nw].mean(), rem=rad[nw:].mean(),
                         wake_real_vs_virtual_r=np.nanmedian(wv)))
RR = pd.DataFrame(rem_rows); RD = pd.DataFrame(rad_rows)
print(RD.round(3).to_string())
print("sessions with at least 100 s of REM:", len(RD), "(paper 26 of 32)")
for cls in ("HD", "FS"):
    d = RR[RR.cls == cls]
    show(signrank(d.r_iso, d.c_iso), f"{cls}, reading (i) WAKE Isomap curve vs REM, against control:")
    show(signrank(d.r_real, d.c_real), f"{cls}, reading (ii) WAKE real-HD curve vs REM, against control:")

print("ed10b, REM vs WAKE radius in the joint embedding:")

Result: reproduced. In 27 sessions with at least 100 s of REM inside the home-cage epochs, REM tuning curves from the virtual HD match WAKE curves above the time-reversed control for HD cells (median r 0.86, |z| = 30.4, n = 1,259) and FS cells (0.43, |z| = 11.4, n = 336), with the WAKE curve from the Isomap angle, and the same with the real-HD WAKE curve (0.82 and 0.36, |z| = 30.3 and 11.5); all p < 1e-29.

fig1ac-posub-border (figshare, data elsewhere)¶

Along a Neuropixel probe crossing pRSC and PoSub, HD tuning of excitatory cells rises in a step at the functional border between the two regions.

The Neuropixel session is figshare Dataset_4.tar.gz (claims file), streamed here. Excitatory cells as for PoSub (rate at least 0.5 Hz in the square epoch, trough-to-peak above 0.4 ms from the file's WaveformFeatures, rate below 10 Hz); HD information from the square-epoch curve at speed above 2 cm/s (file's Velocity). Depth from CellDepth.mat (micrometres), set to 0 at the shallowest cell as the code sets its depth. Running average as Figure_SingleRec_NPX.m: mean HD information in 50 um bins from 0 to -2.5 mm, empty bins interpolated, Gaussian smoothing of 2 bins. The judgement is qualitative (criterion).

In [41]:
# NP, figshare Dataset_4, was streamed in the cell-classes-counts section
tunN = posub.adn_tuning(NP)
ttpN = NP["mat"]["tr2pk"].ravel(); depN = NP["mat"]["cellDep"].ravel().astype(float)
depN = (depN - depN.max()) / 1000
exN = (tunN["rate"] >= 0.5) & np.isfinite(ttpN) & (ttpN > 0.4) & (tunN["rate"] < 10)
print("Neuropixel session", NP["session"], "; units", len(NP["spikes"]), "; excitatory", int(exN.sum()),
      "; depth range (mm)", depN.min(), depN.max(), "; the files' own excitatory count", int(NP["file_types"]["ex"].sum()))
top = -0.05 * np.arange(50); br = np.c_[top, top - 0.05]
prof = np.array([tunN["info"][exN & (depN < a) & (depN >= b)].mean() if (exN & (depN < a) & (depN >= b)).any() else np.nan for a, b in br])
ok = np.isfinite(prof); tt = np.arange(len(prof))
prof_i = prof.copy(); prof_i[~ok] = np.interp(tt[~ok], tt[ok], prof[ok])
prof_s = gaussian_filter1d(prof_i, 2)
mid = br.mean(1)
print("running mean HD information (bits/spike) in every 50 um bin, by bin centre (mm):")
for k0 in range(0, len(mid), 10):
    print("   " + "  ".join(f"{d_:6.3f}: {v_:.3f}" for d_, v_ in zip(mid[k0:k0 + 10], prof_s[k0:k0 + 10])))
for lab, m_ in (("top 1.4 mm (centres above -1.4)", mid > -1.4), ("from 1.8 mm down (centres below -1.8)", mid < -1.8)):
    print(f"{lab}: running mean {prof_s[m_].min():.3f} to {prof_s[m_].max():.3f}")
loc = np.where((prof_s[1:-1] > prof_s[:-2]) & (prof_s[1:-1] > prof_s[2:]))[0] + 1
print("local maxima of the running mean at (mm, bits/spike):", [(round(float(mid[k]), 3), round(float(prof_s[k]), 3)) for k in loc])
dpr = np.diff(prof_s)
k = int(np.argmax(dpr if prof_s[-1] > prof_s[0] else -dpr))
print(f"largest change between adjacent bins at {mid[k]:.3f} mm ({dpr[k]:+.3f}); profile range {prof_s.min():.3f} to {prof_s.max():.3f}; "
      f"shallow third mean {prof_s[: len(prof_s) // 3].mean():.3f}, deep third mean {prof_s[-len(prof_s) // 3:].mean():.3f}")
half = (prof_s.max() + prof_s.min()) / 2
cross = np.where(np.diff(np.sign(prof_s - half)) != 0)[0]
print("crossings of the half-range level at depths (mm):", mid[cross].round(3))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(8, 4))
ax[0].scatter(tunN["info"][exN], depN[exN], s=6); ax[0].set_xlabel("HD info (bits/spike)"); ax[0].set_ylabel("depth (mm)")
ax[1].plot(prof_s, mid); ax[1].set_xlabel("running mean HD info"); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
print("plotted ranges: info", tunN["info"][exN].min().round(3), tunN["info"][exN].max().round(3))
# Which end is which. The files give the depth (CellDepth.mat, cellDep, um) and no probe
# geometry. Figure_SingleRec_NPX.m sets depth = depth - max(depth), so the largest value is the
# top of the profile (0 mm), as here. GetCellTypes_PoSub.m carries, commented out, the line
# "gd(cellDep > 0) = 0; % For the neuropixel rec", which drops the units above cellDep = 0 from
# the PoSub cells: the code's zero is the PoSub border, with PoSub at negative values.
rawN = NP["mat"]["cellDep"].ravel().astype(float)
print(f"cellDep (um): range {rawN.min():.0f} to {rawN.max():.0f}; units above 0: {(rawN > 0).sum()} of {len(rawN)}")
print(f"half-range crossing(s) in the file's units (um): {(mid[cross] * 1000 + rawN.max()).round(0)}")
for lab, m_ in (("cellDep above 0 (pRSC side by the code's line)", rawN > 0), ("cellDep at or below 0 (PoSub side)", rawN <= 0)):
    x = tunN["info"][exN & m_]
    print(f"{lab}: {len(x)} excitatory cells, mean HD information {x.mean():.3f}, median {np.median(x):.3f} bits/spike; "
          f"above 0.2 bits/spike {np.mean(x > 0.2):.2f}")

Result: reproduced (qualitative). Along the figshare Neuropixel probe the running mean HD information of 134 excitatory cells lies between 0.008 and 0.240 bits per spike over the top 1.4 mm (bin centres above -1.4 mm) and between 0.777 and 1.192 from 1.8 mm down, crossing its half-range level once, at -1.675 mm (top third mean 0.074, bottom third 0.940); the profile has a smaller local maximum at -0.625 mm (0.191), and two more at -0.925 mm (0.107) and -1.375 mm (0.240). The crossing lies at cellDep = -35 um in the file's units, next to the code's zero: the commented-out line of GetCellTypes_PoSub.m drops units above cellDep = 0 from the PoSub cells for this recording, so the low end is the pRSC side (71 excitatory cells, mean 0.145 bits per spike) and the high end the PoSub side (63 cells, mean 0.905), as the criterion requires. The files hold no probe geometry, so which end is shallower rests on the code's depth - max(depth), not on the data.

Claims not tested¶

  • fig4-random-connectivity-simulation. A result of simulation. The paper's Python simulation code is not in the figshare item, and the Methods and Supplementary Methods do not give the input tuning widths, the number of inputs or the log-normal weight parameters of each point.
  • fig4h-model-fit. The PyTorch model fit is not deposited, and the Supplementary Methods do not give the numbers of inputs or the initial values.
  • ed6-trn-innervates-adn. Anatomical tracing images, which are neither in the dandiset nor in the figshare item nor anywhere the paper names; recorded as blocked for other, since the claims file marks the claim as data elsewhere and the protocol does not allow data_missing for such claims.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. Python reimplementations of the MATLAB code (tuning curves, HD information, Bayesian decoding, Poisson GLMs by a mirror of glmfit's iteratively reweighted least squares, CCG synapse detection); Isomap from scikit-learn, fitted on at most 4,000 population vectors per session; speed computed from the position, as the files hold no speed series; only lag 0 of the GLM, so pairs are removed for warnings at lag 0 only (four more lags in 9 sessions remove 0.6% more HD-HD pairs); REM restricted to the home-cage epochs; the dandiset's 31 sessions in place of the paper's 32, and 2 of the 5 ArchT mice for the PoSub optogenetic claims (the other three added from figshare in a variant); cue rotation realignment from a Methods-based reimplementation of the code's sigmoid procedure.

What was found about the dataset. The dandiset holds 31 of the paper's 32 PoSub sessions: all 14 vertical ones (931 units, as the paper gives) and 17 of 18 parallel ones (1,760 units against 1,999). The missing one is the Neuropixel session A8603-210602 (239 units, figshare Dataset_4), which the paper's parallel count includes. In three files (A3711, A3717, A3723) the sleep states run to twice the session's length, so that about half of their REM lies after the recording ends, and in three some REM lies inside an exploration epoch (A1821, 16 s in the square and 41 s in the optogenetic epoch; A3712, 12 s in the square; A3701, 0.3 s in the triangle); the REM intervals are the same in version 0.250207.0025. Of the five ArchT mice of the PoSub optogenetic experiment it holds two (A1813, A1815); the other three (A1801, A1804, A1806, six sessions) are on figshare only, as are the ADN, cue rotation and Neuropixel recordings. The optogenetic stimulus series of eight files holds four interleaved channels in one dimension, so its length at the stated 20 kHz is four times the session's; in A1808 it holds one channel of 0 and 1. The dandiset's unit labels (is_excitatory, is_fast_spiking, is_head_direction) follow the code's 0.35 ms cut, not the Methods' 0.4 ms. The files hold no speed series and the probe orientation is given only in the device description.
